### 6. Cost (MEASURED)

**Method.** 640×360 movie runs with the HUD hidden and one held viewpoint. Each row averages 30
samples, frames 100–390. The box is shared with other lanes. The columns:
- process: `Performance.TIME_PROCESS`;
- render CPU / GPU: the viewport's measured render times.

**The variants and order.** A is this branch, B this branch with `SRREVAMP_NO_MAP_ANIM=1`, and C is
dev 8658370 with only the QA print patched in. They ran interleaved A, C, B, twice at each site.

| Site | Run | Process ms | Render CPU ms | Render GPU ms | Sum ms | Draws |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jangan maples (97/168; 456 registered, 123 running) | A1 / A2 | 14.37 / 14.38 | 4.84 / 5.10 | 4.56 / 4.79 | 23.77 / 24.27 | 4,777 |
| | C1 / C2 | 12.73 / 13.29 | 4.88 / 4.87 | 4.70 / 4.70 | 22.31 / 22.86 | 5,336 |
| | B1 / B2 | 13.96 / 12.86 | 5.41 / 4.87 | 5.20 / 4.67 | 24.57 / 22.41 | 5,336 |
| Dunhuang reeds (98/157 at 900, 900; 197 registered, 57 running) | A1 / A2 | 9.91 / 11.56 | 2.01 / 2.28 | 1.89 / 1.91 | 13.81 / 15.75 | 1,655 |
| | C1 / C2 | 5.85 / 6.42 | 2.11 / 2.26 | 1.50 / 1.82 | 9.46 / 10.50 | 1,641 |
| | B1 / B2 | 5.92 / 5.68 | 2.01 / 2.08 | 1.62 / 1.43 | 9.55 / 9.19 | 1,641 |

- **Jangan.** A costs about +1.4 ms against C, all in process time. Render time is equal or lower:
  559 fewer draws, because the animated objects beyond 2,020 are now hidden.
  **Corrected in round 647:** that understates it. At the Jangan spawn (1002, 1020, yaw 0) at
  1280×720 with `--print-fps --disable-vsync`, the rounds 641–646 integration review MEASURED
  14.1–14.5 ms a frame against dev 8658370's 10.6–11.2 ms and 10.9–11.3 ms with
  `SRREVAMP_NO_MAP_ANIM=1` (about +3.3 ms, 90 fps to 70); round 647 MEASURED +2.86 ms (14.05
  against 11.19) and cut it to +0.60 ms. See round 647.
- **Reeds.** A costs about +4.8 ms at 640×360 in those runs, nearly all process time. At 320×180
  in the split runs below it is about +2.9 ms.

#### Where the reeds' cost goes (MEASURED)

The split was made with `MapAnimationProbe`: `SRREVAMP_QA_MAPANIM_SPLIT=420` with
`SRREVAMP_QA_MAPANIM_MODE=<mode>`.
- At frame 420 every registered object is switched to one state, and the driver halts.
- Each run compares the median process time of frames 100–420 against frames 440–800, per frame,
  at the reeds view (98/157 at 900, 900, 320×180, 197 registered, 57 running).
- An `SRREVAMP_NO_MAP_ANIM=1` run (B) gives the drift across the two windows: 6.21 and 6.10.
- The earlier rapid in-run toggling was abandoned: switching skins and players back and forth
  every 12–50 frames swamped the differences.

| Mode (after frame 420) | Before (median ms) | After | Change | Motion after (px, f700 vs f760) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stripped`: players, skeletons and skins gone (the pre-645 object) | 9.10 | 6.37 | −2.73 | 36 |
| `strip_skin`: skins unbound, players and skeletons running | 9.16 | 7.10 | −2.06 | 34 |
| `strip_player`: players freed, skins and skeletons stay still | 9.17 | 8.01 | −1.16 | 29 |
| `freeze_skel`: as `strip_player`, and skeleton processing off | 8.55 | 7.92 | −0.63 | — |
| `share`: every running copy of a clip draws from one skeleton | 8.66 | 8.08 | −0.58 | 26,950 (still moving) |
| `unskin_hidden`: skins unbound on the objects not drawn | 9.07 | 9.05 | 0 | 27,020 |
| `manual`: the driver steps the players itself, timed | 9.02 | 8.63 | — | 26,880 |

Brackets from the same runs: the driver's GDScript loop takes **0.20 ms** a frame (0.05 ms of it the
sector view tests). The 57 players' `advance()` calls take **0.53 ms** (`mix_us`, timed around
manual stepping).

**The split of the ~2.9 ms:**
- **Driver: 0.20 ms** (bracketed).
- **AnimationMixer: 0.53 ms** (bracketed).
- **Skeleton pose and skin-bone updates: about 0.6 ms.** This is what `share` saves, and it matches
  `strip_player` less the mixer.
- **Skinned mesh instances being drawn: about 1.6 ms.** That is `strip_player`/`freeze_skel`
  (8.0 / 7.9) against `stripped` (6.37). It does not depend on the skeleton processing
  (`freeze_skel` equals `strip_player`). It does not come from the skinned objects that are not
  drawn (`unskin_hidden` changes nothing), and the draw count is the same (1,655). So it is the
  cost of the visible skinned instances in Godot 4.2's GL Compatibility renderer, even when their
  pose does not change.
- That process time here includes the render step is INFERRED from these numbers: the monitor's
  split was not read from the engine.

**What was cut: nothing.**
- The largest part, about 1.6 ms, is inherent to Godot's skinned instances. Their pose is the
  object's animation, and drawing them skinned is what makes them move.
- Retail advances every map-object clip every frame by the frame's dt
  (`SWorld::vslot_004` → `CRTAniCyclic::vslot_002`), so a lower rate would change what the player
  sees.
- The one cut that keeps every pose is sharing a skeleton between copies whose clocks are equal.
  It is worth about 0.6 ms. The clocks are equal only while the copies have been in range and in
  view for the same frames, because retail pauses each object on its own. Clock-grouped sharing
  with re-grouping on every pause is left OPEN (TODO.md). The `share` probe itself runs every copy
  in lockstep, so it is not a candidate.
- **B against C.** B now measures like C (Jangan 22.4–24.6 against 22.3–22.9; reeds 9.2–9.6 against
  9.5–10.5), so the A/B switch is clean.

### 2. How retail plays a map object (READ, sro_client.exe)

The addresses and excerpts are in docs/protocol/BSR_FORMAT.md, "How a map object animates".

- **One path for every type.** The compound factory `ResourceMgr::FUN_00be92b0` builds CCompChar,
  CCompBldg or CCompSimple. All three share the animation slots (update 0xc33230, play 0xc2bbb0).
  `FUN_00c2b930` creates the AniMixer only when the `.bsr` has a skeleton **and** at least one
  animation.
- **The clip.** A sector's objects are started by `Map::FUN_00a34140`/`00a342b0`/`00a34a90`, which
  call `Map::FUN_00a38dc0(obj, "default", 0)` (the string is built from 0xd9bac8). So the clip is
  animation group `default`, **action type 0**, and there is **no fallback**
  (`AniMixer::FUN_00c551a0`).
  - Six skeletal models carry only a type-60 entry and do not move in retail:
    `rok_key03..05_01`, `euro_esteuro_viking20`, `big_gate_ja_01` and `fort_stone_ht`. That is
    why 146 of the 152 play.
- **Looping.** The `.ban`'s own IsCyclic word (prim +0x60) picks CRTAniCyclic or CRTAniOneShot. A
  one-shot plays once.
- **Speed and clock.** Speed is 1.0. Time is in ms, wrapping at the `.ban` Duration
  (`CRTAniCyclic::vslot_002` 0xc74790). The authored FPS is unused.
- **Phase.** There is **no random phase**: no `rand()` is on the start path. The clip starts at
  t = 0 when its sector's objects are started.
- **Cull.** `SWorld::vslot_004` (0xa2cf60) updates a list-2 object only while its fade state
  obj+0x1e is not 0 (`SWorld::FUN_00a38a50`). That test is `dist - radius < range`:
  - `dist` is the full 3D distance from the camera (camera struct +0x4);
  - `radius` is `sqrt((dx/2)² + (dz/2)²)` of the object's mesh bounds (asm 0xa389f0);
  - `range` is `DAT_00ec54b0`, 2,500 at start, `min(0.8 × view distance, 2500)`. **Corrected
    in the review follow-up:** the caller subtracts 480.0 first (asm 0xa2d967), so the range is
    2,020. The distance is measured to the placement origin, and the test is strict.

  The update also covers only sectors the view frustum touches. Out of range the clock **pauses**,
  and the object is not drawn either (`Map::FUN_00a1e530`), so the pause cannot be seen. An
  object.ifo flag bit 0 object is updated every frame; 2 of the 146 have it (`rok_key01_01`,
  `naruter_fish01`). No separate animation-LOD distance exists. The every-Nth-frame skip
  (`DAT_01113194`) has no writer, so it is INFERRED off.
- **Skinning.** It is the characters' path: AniMixer, then the runtime skeleton, then
  CObjRendererVS with its SKIN permutations. Whether an unskinned piece of a skeletal object follows
  a bone is OPEN.
- **Tree sway is skeletal.** Round 625's per-mesh word (mesh+0x1f8) is **not** animation: its only
  readers are the object ray test (`FUN_00bd3c50`) and `FUN_00bd3130`, so it marks meshes that take
  ray hits. No wind, sway or wave strings are in the exe, and no wave shader permutation exists.

### 3. What was built (OURS where marked)

- **`client/scripts/world/map_animation.gd` (new).** The PREPARE half reads the `.bsk` and the one
  `.ban` on the objects job's worker. The COMMIT half:
  - gives the template a `Skeleton3D` (`Skeleton3DBuilder.build_skeleton3d`, the characters'
    builder);
  - gives each skinned piece a `Skin` (`build_skin`);
  - adds an `AnimationPlayer` whose `Animation` is built from the `.ban` key times.

  A track whose keys never change is baked into the template skeleton's pose instead of played.
  Tree clips are mostly held poses: a maple is 1 track out of 5 bones, the tentacles 53 tracks out
  of 41 bones × 2.
- **Shared by every placement.** Placements are `duplicate()`s of the template, so they share the
  Animation, the Skins and the meshes. Each owns only its skeleton and its player.
- **The driver.** `MapAnimation.Driver`, one per World3D:
  - it starts each placed clip at t = 0 when the region's objects are placed (READ that retail has
    no phase; OURS that it starts per region, not per sector);
  - it runs a clip only while `dist - radius < 2500` from the camera and the object is in view
    (**corrected in the review follow-up:** 2,020 from the placement origin, a per-sector view
    test, and hidden out of range);
  - ifo flag bit 0 runs at any range.

  The view test is on the object's own bounding sphere, not its sector (OURS: an in-range object
  just off screen keeps its clock in retail and is paused here; neither draws it). The driver tests
  a quarter of the list each frame (OURS, a lag of 4 frames at most; see §4).
- **ObjectLoader.** It keeps each skinned piece's bone palette and calls the two halves.
  - An animated object binds its pieces before any two-pass twin is made, so the twin shares the
    skin.
  - A still object is built exactly as before.
- **What a one-shot shows after it ends** is OPEN. It holds the last key (OURS). (**READ in the
  review follow-up:** retail keeps the last pose too.) This affects the
  horses (`chinaetc_horse*_basic`, IsCyclic 0), several scenery NPCs and nothing else in the census.
- `SRREVAMP_QA_MAPANIM=n` prints `QA MAPANIM frame .. registered running driver_us process_ms`.
  `SRREVAMP_NO_MAP_ANIM=1` leaves everything still, for the A/B.

## Six-hundred-and-forty-fourth round: the Black Robber Den's four bridges and the Temple of fertility's two can be crossed -- the walk on an object goes cell by cell, as the client's does

**The report.** "I can't cross any bridges at the black robber den because an invisible wall
blocks me on all 4 of them", with "invisible bridges" at Hotan north/south and the Fertility
temple. Round 643 takes the drawing; this round the walking.

**Where the den is (READ from `textzonename`).** "Black Robber Den" names regions 91/147-149 and
92/147-149. Its bridges are two `oas_tarim_rob_s_brid` (north and south, 1,311 long) and two
`oas_tarim_rob_b_brid_01` (east and west, 2,664 long) running out from a central tower
(`oas_tarim_rob_b_center`, 700 tall). The Temple of fertility is 101-103/134-135; its bridges are
two `ruin_takla_tembrig_01`. Hotan is 92/135 (`worldmap.ZoneCentre`, round 569); its bridges are
three `oas_hot_b1_bridge` (south, west, east) and `oas_hot_b2_bridge` (north).

**Reproduced by measurement (MEASURED, `client/tools/walk_probe.gd`, headless).** `--cross=1`
is new: a walk carries on into the neighbouring region's graph, re-settling the footing from the
height as `World3D._move_on_nav_graph` does. Each den bridge was walked end to end at dev 8658370:

| bridge | walk | stopped at | on |
|---|---|---|---|
| south | 90/148 (980, 1500) heading 0 | 91/148 (980.0, 477.7) | `oas_tarim_rob_s_brid[1]` |
| north | 93/148 (952, 250) heading 180 | 92/148 (952.0, 1450.5) | `oas_tarim_rob_s_brid[8]` |
| west | 91/146 (1450, 1911) heading 90 | 91/147 (246.3, 1911.0) | `oas_tarim_rob_b_brid_01[14]` |
| east | 91/150 (520, 1909) heading 270 | 91/149 (1718.6, 1909.0) | `oas_tarim_rob_b_brid_01[20]` |

Every stop is on the bridge deck, at about y 620. The edges that stopped them are the bridge's
own. `oas_tarim_rob_s_brid`'s navigation mesh (`--edges`) has a deck at y 617-631 with open ends
(0x00) and 0x10 sides. Under it, on the canyon floor at y 156.5, is a sealed pier footprint:
outline 0x03, x 694.7-1260.4, z 477.7-741.2. The south walk met that footprint's edge at
z = 477.7, 464 units below the deck. The east/west bridge carries two such piers at y 130.9.

This was not a missing mesh, a wrong yaw or position, or a terrain edge. The mover was on the
object, and `NavGraph._first_event` tested **every edge of that object in plan view**, whatever
part of the mesh it bounded.

**The rule, READ in `sro_client.exe` (`/var/tmp/decomp_client`, `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm`).**
- **The in-object walk goes cell to cell** (`CRTNavMeshObj::FUN_0044add0`). It loops `iVar11`
  0..2 over the current cell's edge slots (`CRTNavCellTri::FUN_0045dec0`: `cell+0x28+i*4`),
  skipping the edge it came in by (`param_8`). An open internal edge recurses into its other cell
  (`CRTNavCellTri::FUN_0045ded0`).
- **The slots are filled by the deserializer** (`RTNavMeshObj::FUN_004489b0`). Every edge,
  outline list first and in file order, goes to its `cell_from` cell and, when `cell_to` is not
  0xFFFF, to its `cell_to` cell. Each goes through `RTNavMeshObj::FUN_0045dcf0`, which appends
  while the count at `+0x24` is below 4.
- **So from the deck, the pier's edges are never tested.**
- The entry test for a mover on the terrain (`RTNavMeshObj::FUN_0044a790`) is unchanged. It walks
  the object's own edge grid, which the file stores (`RTNavMeshObj::FUN_00448540`) and which lists
  all 8 of `oas_tarim_rob_b_center`'s outline edges and all 28 of `oas_tarim_rob_s_brid`'s
  (MEASURED, `walk_probe --grid`). The piers still stop someone walking into them on the canyon
  floor, as they should.
- **Which mesh is the navigation mesh** (`FUN_0042ce60` switches on the path's last letter;
  `MapLoader::FUN_0042c4a0` for a `.bsr`):
  - the `.bsr` header word at **0x28** (`mov edi,[esp+0x5c]` at 0x42c73d; the decompiler named
    the wrong local) points at a length-prefixed path;
  - `FUN_0042cbc0` deserializes that one `.bms`'s collision section;
  - a zero word means no navigation mesh;
  - **an empty path is not a zero word** (corrected by the review follow-up, below): the string
    is read and handed on as `""`, and `FUN_0042cbc0("")` opens `data\` through the file
    manager in GFXFileManager.dll, whose answer is not read.

  Rounds 505-643 merged the collision sections of every mesh the `.bsr` lists (OURS, from a
  sweep). `client/tools/navmesh_source_census.gd` over Data.pk2's `navmesh\object.ifo` (3,268
  entries) found the two differ on 4 objects, MEASURED:
  ```
     2039  same single mesh
        3  ours only (EMPTY path at 0x28) euro_esteuro_ph_box2 (word 140), alex_minga07 (132),
                                         alex_fstair02 (133) -- each word points at a length of 0
        1  we merged extra meshes        arabiaf_fpapaya01_03
      105  not a .bsr (cpd)
      817  neither has one
      303  bsr missing
  ```

**Fixed.**
- **`NavGraph` walks an object cell by cell** (`_object_walk`, `_walk_cells`).
  - `NavGraph.place` records each edge's cells (`edge_cell_from`/`edge_cell_to`) and each cell's
    slots (`cell_edges`, the loader's rule: `CELL_EDGE_SLOTS_KEPT` 4, `CELL_EDGE_SLOTS` 3).
  - An on-object mover meets only the edges of the cells its walk crosses. Direction bits are
    judged against the cell it is in, not by side-of-line.
  - The terrain walk and the entry test are unchanged.
- **The mover's cell is inferred, OURS.** The client carries a cell pointer; `_cells_under`
  picks the cell under the point nearest the mover's height, the most clearly containing one
  first.
- **Two guards, OURS.**
  - An edge counts only if the move goes out through it (the cell's centroid on the far side).
  - A walk that meets nothing must end inside the cell it reached; otherwise the next candidate
    cell is tried, and if none explains the move it is stopped where it is. (Review follow-up:
    only candidates at the mover's own level are tried, and a mover with no cell at its level
    under it starts from the nearest ones, `NavGraph._start_cells`.)

  The second was found by this round's own sweep; this entry first said on `cj_field_lamp`,
  through a shared vertex, and that `nav_graph_test` pinned it. **Neither held** (review
  follow-up, below): removing the guard failed no suite, and the guard-removed sweep of 97/168
  leaks on `cj_etc[42]` and `cj_luxury[7]` instead, a mover a hair OUTSIDE a sealed edge after
  a slide. A test that fails without the guard is added below.
- **`World3D._load_object_collision` loads the one mesh** the client does
  (`NavObjectSource.load_collision`, `client/scripts/nav/nav_object_source.gd`). `walk_probe`
  follows whichever rule the build it runs in has, so before/after traces compare like with like.

### Round 644 review follow-up

The review confirmed claims 2 and 3 in the asm, the linked edges (Hotan's castle, bridge and
palace), the negative, and that every zone landing, teleport point and town object cell behaves
as on the base but one. It found a wrong doc, two tests that pinned nothing, two code risks and an
unread parameter. Each is settled here.

**1. The three "no path at 0x28" objects have an EMPTY path, not a zero word (MEASURED, READ).**
`navmesh_source_census.gd` now prints the word and the length it points at:
```
01624 ours only (0x28 word 140, path length 0) euro_esteuro_ph_box2.bsr
02248 ours only (0x28 word 132, path length 0) alex_minga07.bsr
02308 ours only (0x28 word 133, path length 0) alex_fstair02.bsr
```
What the client does with that, READ in `sro_client.exe`:
- `FUN_0043c250` reads a u32 length and resizes the string to it, so a length of 0 gives `""`.
  Nothing between that read and the call to `FUN_0042cbc0` tests the string.
- `FUN_0042cbc0` opens its path through the loader's file manager (loader `+0x28`, vtable
  `+0x28`, access `0x80000000`). When the loader's `+0x14` is 0 it prefixes the path with
  `data\` first (`MapLoader::FUN_0043a3c0`; `cmp [esi+0x14],ebx` at 0x42cc44).
- A failed open returns 0, which means no navigation mesh (0x42cc85, 0x42cd0c).
- So `""` opens `data\`, or `""`. **What that open returns is NOT READ**: the file manager is
  GFXFileManager.dll, not the exe.
- `NavObjectSource` gives the three no mesh. That the open fails is INFERRED: a directory is not
  a file.

It reaches no walk either way (MEASURED). `nav_phantom_census.gd --where=` finds no `.nvm` that
places any of the three, in its own list or as a cross-reference. The same probe finds their
siblings: `alex_fstair01`, `03` and `04`, and `alex_minga01`-`06`/`08`. Alexandria's placed
stairs load the same single mesh on both builds and walk the same. `walk_probe --traverse`,
base 8658370 and this build:
- `alex_fstair01[22]` (90/48): from linked edge 2 to linked edge 30 through 5 cells, 0 walls,
  onto `alex_center`;
- `alex_fstair03[44]`: from open edge 2 to open edge 57 through 11 cells, 0 walls.

So a player climbs the Alexandria stairs as before. `alex_fstair02` with no navigation mesh
changes nothing a player can reach. Whether an `.o2` list draws it somewhere was not checked; if
one does, the player walks the terrain there on either build.

**2. The leak guard is now pinned.** `_inferred_cell_guards` case 1 puts a mover on a sealed box
a hair outside its cell's `0x03` edge, still inside `_triangle_height`'s tolerance, and walks it
on out. With the guard removed from 164b80d (`return {}` unconditionally):
```
FAIL a mover a hair outside a sealed edge of its cell is stopped, not let out through it (z 198.9995, on -1, blocked false)
```
That is the state the real leaks were in (MEASURED, a leak-printing copy of NavGraph with the
guard removed):
- `walk_probe --sweep=400` over 97/168 leaks on `cj_etc[42]` (cell 69, barycentric margin
  -0.000006) and `cj_luxury[7]` (cell 4, -0.000001);
- the 105/80 tent (item 5) leaks at -0.000002.

In each, a slide along the cell's `0x03` outline edge left the mover just past it. The round's
account (`cj_field_lamp`, a shared vertex) did not reproduce, and the old lamp test passes without
the guard; its comment now says so. The slide itself did not reproduce on synthetic shapes: 120
convex sealed heptagons at region-scale coordinates, 72 headings each, gave 0 escapes without the
guard. So the test sets up the state the slide produces, not the slide itself.

**3. The mover's height now picks its part of the mesh, and a test says so.** Case 2 puts a mover
on the pier, under the deck, walking into the pier's sealed side. Against 164b80d with
`_cells_under` ignoring height (`gap := -h`):
```
FAIL a mover on a pier under a deck is stopped by the pier's own sealed side (z 270.000, y 40.00, walls 0)
```
The start cell is now chosen by `_start_cells`, which checks the height twice: the cells under
the point nearest the mover, and a reach test against the step's height. So `gap := -h` alone no
longer fails the test, because the reach test catches the deck 40 up. Ignoring height in both
places (`gap := -h` and the reach test forced true) fails it again, with case 3:
```
FAIL a mover on a pier under a deck is stopped by the pier's own sealed side (z 270.000, y 40.00, walls 0)
FAIL a mover a hair outside the pier's side is stopped there, not walked out and up onto the deck (z 261.0005, y 40.00)
```

**4. No step goes unchecked, and the fallback stays at the mover's level (OURS).**
`NavGraph._start_cells` makes three choices:
- The cells under the point, the one nearest the step's height first. Only those at that cell's
  level are kept: within `LEVEL_REACH` 1.0 of its height there.
- When there is no cell under the point, or the best is more than `SURFACE_REACH_UP` from the
  step's height, it takes the nearest cells of the mover's level in plan instead
  (`_nearest_cells`). The walk from there goes through the guard as usual.
- The step's height is compared with `SURFACE_REACH_UP`, not 1.0, because it is stale within a
  step. A slide substep moves the mover along a ramp without updating it. A first cut compared
  with 1.0, and its 105/80 sweep changed one walk on `euro_esteuro_port01[3]`, where a slide
  began 1.0066 from the step's height (MEASURED); that walk is identical now.

`step_tracked`'s "enter" also takes the crossed edge's own height when the cell under the push is
more than `LEVEL_REACH` from it. That covers a push that lands a hair outside every cell of the
level, or over only a part of the mesh below it. Pinned:
- **Case 4**: a grazing approach to a box's open side a hair from its corner with a sealed side,
  one 5-unit step, as Ghost Walk's `_land` makes one long step. Against 164b80d (and with the
  nearest-cell start removed):
  ```
  FAIL a step whose entry lands a hair outside every cell is still walked, and stopped at the corner (slide true: x 97.002, z 200.1500, entered 0, blocked false)
  FAIL a step whose entry lands a hair outside every cell is still walked, and stopped at the corner (slide false: x 97.002, z 200.1500, entered 0, blocked false)
  ```
  This build stops it at x 99.992.
- **Case 3**: a mover on the pier a hair outside its side, under the deck. The deck's cell
  "explains" the move. Against 164b80d (and with the level filter removed):
  ```
  FAIL a mover a hair outside the pier's side is stopped there, not walked out and up onto the deck (z 261.0005, y 40.00)
  ```

**5. The one new stuck landing is correct (MEASURED).** 105/80 local (1892.2, 649.9) is inside
`ruin_takla_tent05_01[45]`:
- 8 cells and 10 outline edges, every one `0x03`;
- `walk_probe --reach`: 8 of 8 cells reachable, no exit;
- the footing settles on the tent, whose floor is 0.68 below the terrain there.

Walked 40 steps on 16 headings, base and branch end identically on 15. Heading 225 escapes on
the base alone: it slides along outline edge 5, `(1889.0, 643.4)-(1892.3, 638.6)`, until step 37
leaves it at barycentric margin -0.000002 of cell 4, just past that sealed edge. At step 38 it
walks out to the terrain at (1890.7, 639.2). That is the leak of item 2, not a way out. The
client's walk refuses every `0x03` outline edge to a player (item 6), so it would hold them in
the same way. Nothing is hacked round it. How the client settles the footing for a position
that arrives inside a sealed footprint is not read (OPEN, docs/TODO.md).

**6. `collide_mode` is 1 on every walk the client makes (READ).**
- The in-object walk blocks a `0x02`/`0x10` outline edge only when `param_6 != 0`. Otherwise it
  exits through it.
- `param_6` is `CRTNavMeshObj::vslot_002`'s `param_3`. The entry test gets the same value as its
  `param_5`.
- That value is passed on unchanged as the caller's second argument by:
  - the terrain walk 0x4047a0 (`[ebp+0xc]` pushed at 0x404916, 0x404c8d, 0x40511f);
  - the per-instance test (0x4041e3);
  - the dungeon walk (0x43f477);
  - `CRegionManagerBody::vslot_012` (0x412914).
- All nine calls through the region manager at `0x111a02c` push **1**: 0x5068c3, 0x77b791,
  0x9e0ba3, 0x9e0fe0, 0x9e111e, 0x9e12ca, 0x9ed472, 0xa5101c, 0xa54e97.
- The no-slide stop `FUN_004045f0` pushes 1 itself (0x4046f5).

So the branch's rule (0x02/0x10 always holds) matches the client. The cells `--reach` finds with
no exit (`oas_hot_army01`, `euro_esteuro_ph_fbset5_01`, `cj_etc`, the tent) are cells a player
cannot walk out of in the client too. NAVMESH_MOVEMENT.md carries the call chain.

No placed model failed on a `.bsr` or `.bms` the readers refused, and none drew zero triangles.
**So the missing structures were a placement fault, not a loading one.**

### 2. The retail rule (READ, then MEASURED)

- **Both populated lists are built.** `FUN_00a361b0` (MapCallBack.cpp) reads, per sector, a bare
  `uint16` and three counted lists. `lists[0]` goes through `FUN_00a34c50`; `lists[1]` and
  `lists[2]` each go through `Map::FUN_00a1a1d0` into the sector's arrays at +0x14 and +0x24.
  Only byte 27 bit 0 keeps a record out (round 583).
- **One object per key.** `Map::FUN_00a1a1d0` looks the record's key, `CONCAT22(bytes 28-29,
  bytes 22-23)` (the owner region and the uid, round 583), up in a map. It adds one to a found
  entry's count and returns its object; otherwise it calls the map's creator (+0x28) and inserts
  the result.
- **No `.o`.** `strings` over `sro_client.exe` gives `%d\%d.m`, `%d\%d.o2` and `K%d\%d.t`, and
  no `%d\%d.o`; the decompile has the same three.
- **The owner's frame (MEASURED).** 10,703 keys are listed by more than one region, and 10,682 of
  them sit at the identical local position and type in every file; 75,543 of the 75,564 are
  listed by their owner's own file. A record's position is local to its owner region.
  The navmesh loader reads the same frame (READ, review follow-up): `MapLoader::FUN_0042a6e0`
  passes each record's owner to `CRegionManagerBody::vslot_013` (0x412ba0), which returns
  `((region - owner) & per byte) * span`, and subtracts it from the position -- the arithmetic of
  `MapO2Reader.owner_offset`.
- **What was wrong.** 52,366 keys are in `lists[1]` alone, 23,191 in `lists[2]` alone, and 7 in
  both. The seventy-eighth round's reading, "list 2 is a region's own objects; the others
  cross-reference objects belonging elsewhere", held for its sector statistic (91 % against
  46 %), but `lists[1]` is where most of the map lives: a big object is listed by every sector
  it reaches, which is what lowered its figure.

### 3. What changed

- **`World3D.region_placements` (READ rule):** a region's objects are its `.o2`'s `lists[1]`
  and `lists[2]`, skip bit clear, one per key. A neighbour-owned record moves by
  `MapO2Reader.owner_offset`: the owner's second number steps local x and its first steps local
  z, one span each, as `_cell_offset` steps the terrain groups. The `.o` is no longer read, and
  the height filter (`_placements_belonging_here`) and its eight neighbour heightmaps are gone.
  The objects prepare parses the region's own heightmap only, for the grid's cache.
- **`World3D._placed_objects` (READ semantics; the handover is OURS):** a key is placed once in
  the world. The first region to commit it holds it, and later ones share it (`N already placed
  by a loaded region` on the objects line). A region streaming out hands each object it holds to
  another loaded region that lists it, keeping its place (`_release_region_objects`; the log line
  is `region x/y unloaded -- N object(s) it held handed to a region still listing them, M
  dropped`). Retail keeps a refcount instead; the object is drawn while any lister is loaded,
  either way. The registry is cleared with the grid.
- **`MapO2Reader.Entry`** gains `owner_region`, `build_flags`, `skipped()` and `object_key()`,
  and `mapo.Entry2` gains `OwnerRegion()`, `Skipped()` and `Key()`.
- **`SRREVAMP_QA_OBJECTS`**: at each `--shots` viewpoint, one `QA OBJECT` line per matching
  placed object -- its key, the holding region, its position, pieces, triangles, visibility and
  frustum -- counted from the drawn surfaces' own index arrays.
- `foliage_census.gd --near` and `probe_seasonal.gd` follow the same rule.
- **`_qa_float_report` (review item 4):** it walked each region's container and measured
  against the holding region's ground. Since the key handover, a container can hold a
  neighbour's object, whose ray lands on the owner's ground, so such objects were skipped. It
  now walks `_placed_objects` and measures each object against its owner region's terrain, in
  that region's space.
  - It prints `(N measured, K of them held by a region other than their owner; M skipped:
    owner region not loaded)`.
  - Hotan, `--radius 1`, `SRREVAMP_QA_FLOAT=4000`: `0 placed object(s) ... (132 measured, 5 of
    them held by a region other than their owner; 12 skipped: owner region not loaded)`.
  - Those 5 were skipped before.

### 3a. The second object source: `force_addobject.txt` (review follow-up; READ unless marked)

The review found a second path that places map objects, and that the round had dropped three
bridges the report was about.

**The path** (full chain, addresses and layout in MAPO2_FORMAT.md, "Round 643's review"):
Client_LoadAllRefData loads Media.pk2's `server_dep\silkroad\textdata\force_addobject.txt`
(`Client_LoadRefDataFile` type 0x3d), then `FUN_00927620` → `SWorld::vslot_045` → the tail of
`FUN_00a361b0`.
- A row with service 0 is not loaded. 35 of the file's 55 rows load: 32 `fortress_flag` and 3
  `bagh_masin_bridge01` at 124/247 (FORTRESS_BIJEOKDAN).
- Each loaded row becomes an object of region `(regionY << 8) | regionX` when that region's
  `.o2` loads. It is keyed by (region, `int(z)/320 & 7` in uid bits 13-15, `int(x)/320 & 7` in
  bits 10-12, and a per-sector counter from 0x3ff down).
- It goes through the same cache and creator as the `.o2` records. The creator
  (`FUN_00a33530`) copies the record verbatim, **so the Y is the row's own**.
- The path is found in the object-path table case-insensitively (`CompareStringA`,
  `NORM_IGNORECASE`). `fortress_flag.bsr` is not in `object.ifo`, and `vslot_045` appends such a
  path as a new type.

**The Y: 848 against 53.7 (READ, then MEASURED).**
- The `.o2` lists the three bridges in `lists[1]` with **the skip bit set** (7cf7#5121, #18433
  and #40961, Y 53.7 / 52.8 / 53.7), so the map loader does not build them. The force rows build
  them at Y 848.
- The model's drawn vertices span local y -1686.2 .. -784.4: piers down to the ravine floor.
  At Y 848 its top is at 63.6.
- The `.nvm` lists the three at Y 53.7, with the bridge's own navmesh a plane at local y 5.3,
  so the walkable deck is at 59.0.
- At dev's Y 53.7 (from the `.o`), the drawn top sits at -730.6: 790 under the walkable deck
  and 19 above the heightmap (-749.1).
- So the two numbers are two copies of one bridge: the drawn object at 848, the navigation copy
  at 53.7. Dev "drew" the bridges, but buried in the ravine. That is the invisible bridge the
  user describes, and the review's "regression" was a drop from buried to absent.

**Collision:** this path attaches none (the creator copies the record only). The walkable deck
is the `.nvm`'s object, which the navigation code already reads. The drawn bridge carries the
trimesh every placed object carries.

**The fortress state: OPEN, not READ.**
- Creation and the insert into the sector's list-1 array are unconditional (READ).
- For an object whose +0x37 word (`type << 24 | guild << 16 | fortress`) is neither 0 nor -1,
  the loader calls the world's callback (world+0x7b34, installed through `SWorld::vslot_011` as
  `LAB_004ff8c0`). On add, that callback:
  - for a flag, sets a texture from the guild's or the alliance's emblem (object vtable+0x104,
    `FUN_00789300`);
  - for a structure, looks the fortress up (`FUN_00938a10`) and calls `FUN_0052d4e0` with
    arguments chosen by the fortress record's +0x20 bits. `FUN_0052d4e0`'s shape is a clip
    lookup and play (INFERRED).
- No visibility write was found, but the vtable calls were not followed. So whether a fortress
  state hides a row is OPEN.
- This client draws every loaded row, the flags with their own texture and no emblem (OURS).
  The code says so at `ForceAddObjectReader` and `World3D._force_rows_for`.

**Implemented:**
- `ForceAddObjectReader` (`client/scripts/mapo/force_addobject_reader.gd`): `parse`,
  `rows_for`, `uid_for` and `placements`.
- `World3D._force_rows_for`: the table is read once per world from Media.pk2. A region's rows
  are handed to its objects job on the main thread, and `_objects_prepare` appends them only
  when the region's `.o2` loads, as the READ tail does.
- `placement_model_path`: a row whose path the index lacks is drawn by its own path.
- `server/cmd/mapobjcensus -media` adds the rows to the retail set.

## Six-hundred-and-forty-second round, review follow-up: a teleport is served only within the retail interaction range, never from an instanced gate, and walking away closes the gate's talk box

The review confirmed round 642's READ claims. It also verified with real input a paid non-GM ferry
(gold 1000 -> 500) and the level-95 refusal at the harbour, so the TODO item for a charged teleport
under real input is closed. Labels as before. The record is in `docs/protocol/teleport_network.md`,
"The interaction range (round 642's review)".

**READ: the interaction range.** `HandleTeleportUse` (`0x513590`) calls
`GObjPC::IsWithinInteractionRange` (`0x4a8e10`) before the id-8 check and the link, and refuses
with its return value.
- **3** when the object's TypeID fails the mask: `0x146` (NPCNPC) or `0x30` (structure), in
  `FUN_004a8d90`.
- **3** when the regions are not both field or both dungeon, or differ by 2 or more on either byte
  (`FUN_00430ce0`).
- **4** when the 3-D length is over the class's limit. The length comes from `FUN_00430ba0`: local
  difference plus 1920.0 times the region-byte difference, region y on x and region x on z. The
  limits, read from the exe's `.rdata`, are:
  - IsPC 600, IsNPCNPC **300**, IsMonster 500, IsCOS 1500;
  - IsStruct **800**, IsItem 10, IsPet 500, default 320.

The client's category 0xd shows 4 as `UIIT_MSG_INTERACTION_FAIL_TOO_FAR` (`0x7ba03b`) and nothing
for 3.

**Fixed:**
- **The range on the server.** `teleport.Reach` and `session.teleporter.reach` apply it before
  the link, from the object's place:
  - a gate structure's teleportbuilding row, limit 800;
  - an NPC's npcpos rows, limit 300, nearest row. cmd/server records them from `-npcpos-csv`
    (`teleportObjectPlaces`).

  `worldmap.FromWorld` names the hub position back into region and local coordinates.
  - OURS: the height term is dropped. The server does not know the player's height: an arrival
    holds y = 0 and the client sends no move after landing.
  - OURS: an NPC with no npcpos row is not measured, and the boot log warns.
  - The stale second request that round 603's review left open is now refused 3, with nothing
    charged.
- **The source world (OURS).** A gate point whose `WorldID` is not 1 is refused with code 0.
  - 64 retail links leave such a point.
  - Round 642's retail-link test had counted 46 of them as moved. It now counts them as refused.
- **The old export.** A teleport directory whose points all read `WorldID` 0 logs a boot warning.
  That is an export from before round 642, and with it the instance refusal is off.
- **Client, plausible:**
  - A gate's or teleport NPC's talk box closes when the player walks beyond the same limit, in 3-D
    (`World3D._check_talk_range`, `talk_out_of_range`). Other NPCs' talk boxes are left open: their
    range is not read. This also stops a far bank's lines being clicked again and again.
  - The refusal text is the archive's `UIIT_MSG_INTERACTION_FAIL_TOO_FAR` for 4, and our own words
    for 3.
  - `/where` reports `NetClient.current_zone`, the zone after a zone change or teleport, instead of
    the entry's.
- **Comments.** The stale "no range test" comments are corrected: `teleport.go`'s header and three
  in `World3D.gd`.

## Six-hundred-and-forty-second round: the ferries, airships, tunnels and every other teleport NPC take a player to their linked point

The user asked for every teleport NPC across the map to work and to go to the right place. The
examples were the river ferries and the way to the Roc Mountain region. The whole record is in
`docs/protocol/teleport_network.md`, "Teleport NPCs (round 642)". Labels: READ = recovered from a
binary, MEASURED = counted or run, INFERRED = argued from shape, OURS = this project's choice.

**Before (MEASURED on dev 8658370).** 32 NPCs are the associated object (teleportdata column 3) of a
point with links. The census:
- 8 ferry and boat sellers, 7 airship sellers, 4 tunnel managers;
- the Constantinople harbour, the two pirates and the Paros Light House harbour;
- Jangan's four `[Teleport]` gate soldiers and Constantinople's three guides;
- the two NPCs that lead to Thief Town.

All 32 are placed by npcpos. None worked:
- the server refused every one with code 2, "no such gate". `session.gateBuilding` required a
  teleportbuilding row, and its own comment said "a ferry point is not a gate";
- the client offered no teleport line. `_npc_services` looked the code up only as a building.

**READ (server, `/var/tmp/srgs.asm` and the dump):**
- **An NPC is served as a gate is.** `RefTeleport_ExtractData` sets `+0x190` of any associated ref
  object to the teleport record (`0x6a7ce7`), with no class test.
  - `HandleTeleportUse` requires the talked-to object to offer interaction 8, 0x1c, 9 or 0x1e
    (`FUN_00485d00`, refusal 3).
  - It then takes the link through `+0x190`.
- **Id 8's registrar, settled.** This was `character_state.md`'s open discrepancy.
  - `FUN_006b5200` builds the 0x1c-byte `_REFTELELINK` link, which `FUN_006a7460` fills.
  - It calls `0x6a7f70` with EAX = the link's source `CRefTeleport` (`FUN_004f89f0`, `0x6b527c`).
  - So id 8 goes on a source point's object when that point's `+0x34` byte is 1. The byte is the
    last one `0x6a7be0` reads, and the client's `teleportdata.txt` has no column for it.
  - Stand-in, disclosed on both sides: a point with an outgoing link offers id 8.
- **The arrival is the point, exactly.** `0x407760`, called through `0x4e0a40` at `0x513779` with
  the link's target, copies the region word and x/y/z words, with no radius term. The one radius
  scatter in the server is the battle arena's `FUN_00662380`. This replaces round 576's
  "arrival is an inference".
- **teleportdata column 12 is the destination's game world.** `0x407760` hands the `+0x48` word to
  `GameWorldMgr_FindByID` (`0x5137ac`; no world means refusal 2, `0x513802`), and `0x6a7be0`
  stores it at `0x6a7f21`. The word is READ.
  - The column is INFERRED to be that word, from its position and its values: 1 on all 153
    open-world rows, 2/4/7 on the fortresses, 40 on Roc, 57-60 on the tombs and temples, 95-170 on
    the arenas and survival.

**Fixed:**
- **Server.** `session.gateObject` serves a point whose object is an NPC, and still refuses a
  point with no object.
  - A destination whose `WorldID` is not 1 is refused with code 0 and nothing charged (OURS: one
    world). It is checked after the restrictions and before the charge.
  - `teleport.Point.WorldID` is the export's new twelfth column. An 11-column CSV still loads, with
    WorldID 0.
  - New lookups: `Table.PointByObject` and `Table.BuildingByID`.
- **Client.**
  - `TeleportReader.point_for_object` and `World3D._teleport_point_for_code` find a point by
    building code or by NPC id, through the reverse of `_npc_codes`.
  - A ferry seller's talk box reads "1. Select a teleport area:", then the end line. Its list is
    the point's links, in file order, with their fees.
- **QA.**
  - `SRREVAMP_QA_CLICK=npc:<CODE>` targets a named NPC, retrying while its region streams in.
  - `SRREVAMP_QA_AIM_ONLY` stands the player and prints the click point instead of dispatching.

  - `SRREVAMP_QA_COMMANDS` takes `wait <s>`.

**Directions (MEASURED over the export).** Every link out of an NPC point has its reverse, except
the two into Thief Town (`7 -> 8`, `34 -> 8`), whose destination has no link out. So there was no
one-way link to fix. 62 of the 292 retail links are one-way. srrevamp adds none.

## Six-hundred-and-forty-first round: the chat and the system log hide their frames when the mouse is away, and the chat's lock button keeps the chat's frame shown

The user asked for retail's auto-hide on the two bottom windows. Their screenshot shows both
windows hidden: the lines float at the bottom left and the bottom right, with no frame, tabs or
background. The chat's second top-left icon, whose tooltip is "Lock Chat window/Auto hide",
switches it. The system log is to keep auto-hide always on. Everything below was read from
`sro_client.exe` on the box. The full reading, with addresses, is in `docs/protocol/chat.md`
("Auto-hide") and `docs/protocol/system_message.md` ("Auto-hide").

**READ:**
- **One test, every frame.** CGInterface's update (`vslot_012`, `0x77b140`) asks each window
  whether its frame is wanted:
  - the chat (`0x7a9d10`): the mouse inside its rect, or its input line holding the keyboard
    (`0x634ea0`), or the mouse inside the whisper list's rect, even hidden;
  - the system window (`0x7b85a0`): the mouse inside its rect, or inside the filter board's rect
    while the board is shown.

  The rect test `0xb8f3d0` is inclusive at both edges. There is no delay and no fade: the update
  calls each control's show (vslot 0x5c) directly, and CIFWnd's show (`0x652b70`) starts no timer.
- **What hides.**
  - Chat (`0x7a9bd0`): the bands, the tabs and their lamps (`0x7a9a80`), the scroll bar, the two
    top-left buttons, the size button, the chat-mode button and the input box.
  - System window (`0x7b84e0`): the bands, the filter button, the size button, the scroll bar
    (unless mode 1) and an open filter board.
  - Neither touches its lists, so the lines stay, with their shadow and no background.
- **The lock.** It is `GDR_BUTTON_CHATTABHIDE` (ID 12, `chat_hide_button.ddj` at 30,0), with the
  tooltip UIIT_STT_CHATING_VIEW_AUTO_OFF (`0x7ac168`).
  - Its handler `0x7a99b0` only flips the byte +0x48c; shown = locked or wanted.
  - The constructor sets the byte to 0 (`0x7ad3e4`), so auto-hide starts on.
  - Only the constructor, the toggle and the update's getter touch it: it is not saved, and the
    button's art does not change with it.
- **The system window's switch** is the game option `settings+7`, "System UI Autohide"
  (UIIT_MSG_SYSTEM_WND_HIDEMSG). It is saved in `Setting\SROptionSet.dat` as tag 0x7d8
  (`0x502cb2`). That settles round 639's OPEN "hover-only option".

**MEASURED:** the box's `SROptionSet.dat` holds 1 for tag 0x7d8 (on).

**INFERRED:** that `0xb8f3d0`'s insets (+0x50..+0x5c) are the ClientRect. They are 0 for both
windows.

**OURS:**
- The system window's auto-hide is always on, at the user's request (`HudSystemMessage.AUTO_HIDE`).
- Godot will not focus a hidden control. So Enter and R's reply show the chat's frame before
  focusing the line: the same frame, one update early.
- The lock's state lives only in the window (`HudChat.locked`), as in retail.
- A mouse event also runs the frame test at once, at its own position (`HudChat.FrameWatch`, a
  child node, because the chat's `_input` name is its line edit). A click that arrives with the move
  into the window then finds the line shown. Retail tests only once a frame; with a real mouse the
  move comes first either way.
  - This is also what lets pushed clicks reach the line in the headless suites
    (`hud_keys_after_chat_test`, `hud_stack_test`): a headless viewport reports its centre as the
    mouse position.
  - Without it, those two suites failed ("clicking the chat's input line focuses it").

**Built.**
- **`HudChat`.** `update_frame` runs from `_process` on the real mouse, with `frame_wanted`,
  `set_frame_shown`, `toggle_lock` and the three buttons' READ tooltips. Mode and frame visibility
  are now applied in one place (`_apply_visibility`). Enter and R's reply work while the frame is
  hidden: `can_open` tests the window, not the line.
- **`HudSystemMessage`.** The same `update_frame`, with the board rule and the mode-1 scroll rule.
- **The log.** Each window prints `CHAT FRAME` / `SYSTEM FRAME` with its rect when its frame
  changes, and `CHAT LOCK` when the lock is pressed.

**Real input on the box** (Login -> CharacterSelect, xdotool, 1280x720; the dev server in memory;
`/var/tmp/autohide/e2e`; screenshots in the session's `autohide_shots/`). The client's own log, in
order:

    CHAT FRAME hidden rect=[P: (2, 477), S: (399, 175)]       (the mouse on the world)
    SYSTEM FRAME hidden rect=[P: (923, 513), S: (350, 117)]
    CHAT FRAME shown ...                                       (hover the chat)
    CHAT FRAME hidden ...
    SYSTEM FRAME shown ... / SYSTEM FRAME hidden               (hover the log, then away)
    CHAT FRAME shown ...                                       (Enter, the mouse away)
    CHAT SEND: type 3 index 1 to '': hello_autohide            (typed and sent; still shown)
    CHAT FRAME hidden ...                                      (Escape)
    CHAT FRAME shown ... / CHAT LOCK on (auto-hide off)        (hover, click the lock, away: stays)
    CHAT LOCK off (auto-hide on) / CHAT FRAME hidden ...       (click again, away: hides)
    CHAT FRAME shown ... / CHAT FRAME hidden ...               (a click on the line straight from the
                                                                world focuses it; Escape, away)

The screenshots show what `autohide.png` shows: the chat line bottom-left and the log's lines
bottom-right, bare with their shadow. The hover over the lock shows its tooltip, "Lock Chat
window/Auto hide". (Pictures for a human; the log lines above are the measurement.)

**Tests.** `client/scripts/ui/hud/hud_autohide_test.gd` has 40 checks on synthetic layouts: what
hides and what stays; the inclusive rect; the whisper-list rect; Enter and Escape through
`push_input`; R's reply; the lock and its tooltip; mode 0; the system window's board and mode-1
rules; a pushed mouse move. The negative, against dev 8658370 with the new test copied in:

    FAIL the lock's tooltip is UIIT_STT_CHATING_VIEW_AUTO_OFF's (got )
    FAIL HudChat has update_frame()
    FAIL HudChat has frame_wanted()
    FAIL HudChat has set_frame_shown()
    FAIL HudChat has toggle_lock()
    FAIL HudSystemMessage has update_frame()
    FAIL HudSystemMessage has frame_wanted()
    FAIL HudSystemMessage has set_frame_shown()
    FAILURES: 8

**OPEN:**
- the retail default of "System UI Autohide" with no settings file;
- the Game options checkbox, which srrevamp does not offer, by the user's choice;
- the whisper list (ID 51) and its button, not built.

**Review follow-up.**
- **The edge pixel.** `0xb8f3d0` is inclusive, but Godot's hit test is half-open, so a click on
  x = end.x reached the world. Both windows now override `_has_point` with the inclusive test.
- **Log noise.** `CHAT FRAME` / `SYSTEM FRAME` print only with `SRREVAMP_QA_FRAME_LOG` set.
  `CHAT LOCK` stays.
- **The update's cadence.** Retail calls `0x7a9bd0(1)` on every frame while the frame is wanted and
  unlocked (`0x77b407`). Its show returns early when nothing changes (`0x652b70`), so calling only
  on a change is equivalent. Noted in chat.md.
- The test now has 42 checks.

**Checks.**
- Client: `check` loads 402 scripts, and `tests` runs 162 suites with 0 failing.
- Go: build, vet and `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` pass (60 packages ok; no server change).

## Rounds 636-640 integration review (feat/walls): a death ends the wall on the default respawn path, a re-bound hotbar slot takes its level's code, and the wall's refusal tests 'tel2' and 'tel3'

The final review of feat/walls (dev 5a82339 + rounds 636-640 and their follow-ups, at b38b358) read
the unreviewed commits (76cb92d, b38b358, 3bbe05a) and the merges, and ran two clients through
Login with real input against a server built from the branch: buff stacking, `/speed`, remote
facing and the arrival list's headings, the target row with the premium, EXP in the system
window, the hotbar across relogs and an upgrade, the doll's ten clicks, and the walls (the root,
attacks while rooted, the absorb to the break, the drain, the toggle-off, Ghost Walk refused). No
SCRIPT ERROR in six logs. It found these; all are fixed here. Before is b38b358.

**1. A death on the default path left the wall up (OURS rule, now applied on both paths).** With
`-player-dead-state` off -- the deploy default -- `monsterStrike` respawned a killed player without
ending the book; only `markDead` (the dead-state path) did. A player killed through Crystal Wall
(physical only) by magical blows respawned still walled: rooted, in state 0x11 (no regen), drained
41 MP every 5 s. MEASURED with a throwaway test on b38b358: `dead-state false, died true, HP now 80,
rooted true, motion 0x11, records 1`. The respawn path now calls `endBuffsOf` under the kill lock,
as `markDead` does (kill lock, then buff lock). Every buff ends there now, as on the dead-state
path (round 616's rule, OURS: the retail death rule was not traced). `rv636_640_test.go`
`TestRound640ADeathOnTheRespawnPathEndsTheWall` kills Aria through Crystal Wall and wants the
wall's OpBuffEnd, no records, no root, STAND and a move that goes through; against b38b358 it
fails `waiting for 0x00F6: ... i/o timeout`.

**2. A re-bound hotbar slot kept the old level's code (round 639).** `HotbarStore.rebind_for_skill`
changed a slot's id and kept its code: live, slot 6 became `{1287, SKILL_CH_LIGHTNING_GYEONGGONG_B_01}`
and was saved so. It takes `new_code` now, the new id's own Basic_Code (skilldata column 3 of that
level's row, `SkillBuffCatalog.info(id)["basic_code"]`, `World3D._skill_basic_code`); an empty code
(the index not ready) keeps the slot's, as before. `hotbar_store_test.gd` checks the learn and the
withdrawal re-binds and the empty-code fallback. (Casting was not affected: the clip name drops the
level suffix.)

**3. The wall's 0x3009 refusal tested 'tele' alone.** `Skill_CheckUseConditions` refuses a row
carrying `tele`, `tel2` or `tel3` while the book holds a wall (READ, `srv.asm` 0x58e033..0x58e061:
`cmp [edx+0x1dc],0`, then `+0x2ec`, `+0x2f0`, `+0x2f4`, each `jne 0x58dae4`, `mov ax,0x3009`);
`refdata.Skill.HasTele` read only `tele`. The export now carries `tel2`/`tel3` presence as CSV
columns 87/88 (`teleColumns`, a strict suffix: an older CSV loads false), the SQL store keeps them,
and the gate asks `Skill.HasTeleport`. `HasTele` -- the ground-cast move -- is unchanged, so no EU
row starts moving. MEASURED on the box's Media.pk2 (60 plain skilldata shards, 33,709 ids, every
Param walk finished, the literal words agree): `tel2` on 7 rows
(SKILL_EU_WIZARD_PSYCHICA_TELEPORT_A_01..03, _B_01..02, SKILL_EU_WARLOCK_PSYCHICA_TELEPORT_A_01,
SKILL_EU_BARD_PSYCHICA_TELEPORT_A_01), `tel3` on 21 (SKILL_EU_WARRIOR_FRENZYA_TOUNT_SPRINT_A_01..21),
`tele` on 20. All `tel2`/`tel3` rows are EU skills, so a walled Chinese caster meets the refusal
through Ghost Walk; the fix makes the gate match the read rule. `TestTeleColumns` (export ->
import -> HasTele/HasTeleport) and `TestRound640ATel2RowIsRefusedWhileWalled` (a `tel2`-only row
refused while walled; against the old `HasTele` gate it answers "select a location on the ground").
**Deploy:** the refusal for `tel2`/`tel3` rows needs a re-export of the skill CSV; an old CSV
behaves as before.

**Not changed (noted by the review).** The skill window's click assigns `BaseSkill.basic_code` for
any learned level, as before; only the rebind now writes the level's own code.

**Checks.** Go: build, vet and `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` pass (shared cache). Client: `check`
loads all 401 scripts; `tests` runs 161 suites, 0 failing.

The review confirmed, in both binaries, that nothing roots a walled caster. So the root stays OURS,
at the user's request. It also confirmed the `pw` meanings, the wall HP, the `onff` drain, 0x11 and
the lifecycle. Labels as before; the detail is in `docs/protocol/skill_buffs.md`, "The protection
walls".

**READ:**
- **Ghost Walk.** While the caster's book holds a wall (`book+0x1dc`), `Skill_CheckUseConditions`
  refuses a row carrying `tele`, `tel2` or `tel3` with 0x3009 (0x58e033..0x58e061). This runs
  before the cooldown test and the motion gate. It is retail's own rule, now in `useSkillHandler`
  (`wallTeleRefusal`, OURS text). It replaces round 640's OURS ground-move refusal.
- **The wall is charged before the absorb test.** The entry's `+0x10 = 1` is written at 0x58f00b
  and `+0x18 += damage` at 0x58f015, both before 0x58f03e.
  - `buff.Books.HitWall` now does the same: a blow sharing a type with the wall charges it, and
    only then is absorbed or not.
  - A mixed 4|8 blow would split. No `att` row has both bits (MEASURED), so srrevamp's blows never
    do.
  - A blow of no `att` type is absorbed at no cost to the wall, since both twins return 0.
- **The imbue term.** The absorb test's second term is the attacker's imbue: the context's `+0x78`
  comes from `book[0x79]`, is gated by `att[4]` and scaled by `att[4]/100`. It is named, not
  modelled: srrevamp's monsters carry no imbue.
- **Client (kind 7 and DefenseEfp).** A kind-7 number is always display type 0, never the critical
  style. The DefenseEfp is READ (`FUN_00a9c470` files column 13, "DefenseEfp", at +0x80) and plays
  with any attached skill deco; with none, the attacker's DamageEfp plays. srrevamp stands
  HitEffect's default in for that DamageEfp (OURS: the monster's skill is not on the wire).
- **Doc corrections.**
  - The toggle-off runs after phase 0's 0x3003/0x3030 refusals. `FUN_0059ef90` matches a
    sub-state-1 record. `FUN_0059eff0(0)` only zeroes its end flag `+0x10`; the book update ends it.
  - The client's 500 ms lock is set by the 0x7074 senders, through `FUN_009eb130`.
- **OPEN, not modelled.** srrevamp has none of these:
  - summons, mercenary scrolls and mounting, all refused while walled (0x4931d6, 0x49be6f,
    0x49b507, 0x4fc52a);
  - knockback and knockdown, skipped on a walled target (0x58fee5, `FUN_0058e540`).

  Potions are not refused.

**Fixed:**
- **The drain race.** The drain now re-reads the due records under the owner's buff lock, after the
  store read. A toggle a cancel, recast or break ended meanwhile is not charged.
- **Broken-wall order.** The strike that breaks a wall ends it after its own messages. The toggle
  ticker leaves a wall broken within `buff.BrokenGrace` (1 s, OURS) alone, so the end never overtakes
  the report.
- **Performance.** `monsterStrike` checks for a wall before `monsterBlowType`, so an unwalled
  player's blow never reads the skill table.
- **Toggle-off.** The server's answer decides: a toggle-off reply ends any cast the client drew.
- **The root's desync (OURS).** A move the root drops is answered to the mover alone with an
  `OpSkillMove` carrying the wall's skill and the position the server holds. The client snaps back
  (`ROOT: the server holds this player at ...`).
- **ghost_walk_test** compared whole aniset rows, which now carry `priority` (and `defense`). It
  compares the lists and the group.

**The wire.** Merged `int/r640` (rounds 637-639): the wall suffix now follows round 639's 16-byte
EXP tail on `OpAttackResult`. Both decoders read it at offset 59.

**Tests.**

## Six-hundred-and-fortieth round, the root: a wall roots its caster (OURS, the user's choice)

Round 640 found nothing in either binary that roots a walled caster. Asked, the user chose **"Root
while walled"**. It is built as **OURS**, not retail's, and labelled so in the code
(`session/walls.go` `wallRoots`, `World3D._wall_root`), in `docs/protocol/skill_buffs.md` and in
`docs/TODO.md`.
- **Server:** while a `pw` record is active on the caster's book (`buff.Books.HoldsWall`), an
  `OpMove` is dropped silently in `motions.moved`, the way a move in the sit/stand transition is.
  A Ghost Walk cast is refused before any cost (OURS text: "cannot move while a wall is up").
- **Client:** while its own wall buff stands (the catalog row carries `pw`), no move is started
  and there is no walk clip. That covers a ground click, a held-button steer, and the walk into an
  attack's, a friendly cast's or a pick-up's reach. Each refusal is logged as `ROOT: ... refused --
  this player's wall (skill N) roots it (OURS ...)`. Attacks, casts and pick-ups go out from where
  the player stands, and the server's reach rule answers them. A walk already under way stops.
- **The end:** it ends with the wall's record: a right-click cancel, a recast, the wall's HP at 0,
  the MP drain running short, a death or a logout.

  - The negative against 946da3a:

## Six-hundred-and-fortieth round: Fire Wall and Crystal Wall take the blows of their type until their own HP runs out, drain MP until it runs short, and switch off when recast or cancelled

The user's request: "There's also skill lines like fire wall and crystal (ice) wall that don't let
you move but you can attack within a certain radius. You have to cancel those skills to be able to
move or have those walls run out of hp (not player hp)."

Labels: READ (`SR_GameServer.exe` -- the dump and `srv.asm` on the RE box -- and `sro_client.exe`,
the dump and `sro_client.asm`), MEASURED (the retail export), INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The rules with
every address are in `docs/protocol/skill_buffs.md`, "The toggles" and "The protection walls".

**1. What `pw` is (READ).** Round 636's hand-off had `pw` 11,1159,0,17 (Fire Wall - Tower lv1) and
7,824,0,11 (Crystal Wall lv1), with value[1] "likely the wall's HP". All four are now read:
- value[0], the damage types the wall covers: bit 4 physical, bit 8 magical -- the same bits as
  `att` value[0]. So Fire Wall (11) covers **magical** blows and Crystal Wall (7) **physical** ones;
  the tooltips agree ("Absorbs the magical attack by creating a wall of fire", MEASURED).
- value[1], the wall's HP: EngageSkill (`0x593540`) builds the wall object at ctx `+0x5c` with it.
- value[2] and value[3], the wall's flat defence and defence percent: the two mitigation twins
  `FUN_0040ebe0` / `FUN_0040eef0` (filed as `Formula_Mitigate{Physical,Magical}DamageOnWall`) run
  the ordinary formula with them in place of the defender's params 5 and 7.
- The holder is the **target** (`pc+0xc0c`), which settles skill_params.md's open question.

**2. A blow on a walled caster (READ).** `Combat_ResolveDamage` builds a second, kind-7 entry for
the wall while its HP is not 0 and resolves the blow against the wall's own defence. When the blow's
types are ones the wall covers, the caster's own entry is marked 8 and skips everything: no block
roll, no mitigation, no wear, no damage. `Combat_ApplyActionEffects` then takes the damage off the
wall (`if (HP < dmg) HP = 0; else HP -= dmg`). A blow of another type leaves the wall alone and lands
on the caster as usual. The next book update ends a wall whose HP is 0 (0xB072) and resets the
motion. **So yes: the wall's HP drops and the caster's does not, until the wall breaks.**

**3. The toggle (READ).** Every `onff` row -- the 55 walls and 61 Bard songs and dances, 116 in all
(MEASURED) -- has no `dura` and is drained by `SkillAction_Buff`'s sub-state 2: onff[1] MP each
time more than onff[0] ms have passed; with less MP than that, the buff ends (a pool of exactly the
cost pays it, to 0). A recast of a running `onff` skill **ends it** (`Tick_UseSkill` phase 0,
0x4ae622..0x4ae64d) before the gate, the cost and the cooldown -- that is how retail "cancels" a wall
from the hotbar; the buff bar's right-click is the dispel round 616 built.

**4. The motion state (READ).** EngageSkill sets 0x11 SKILL_PROTECTIONWALL (no broadcast). In it
the gate refuses another `ao`/`pw` skill, the sit key does nothing and the regen tick restores
nothing. MEASURED in the run below: MP fell by exactly 58 every 5 s while standing walled.

**5. What was NOT found: anything that roots the caster.** The user remembers the walls stopping
movement and allowing attacks "within a certain radius". Neither binary does that, by these probes:
- Server: the movement handler `GObjPC::FUN_004b0ea0` (slot 377, CGObjPC's too -- vtable 0xaf59fc
  read) refuses motion states 8, 0x10 and 0x12, the `stns` stun holder `pc+0xc44`, a running action,
  abnormal bits and a failed path -- **no compare with 0x11 anywhere in 0x4b0ea0..0x4b11f9**. The
  hand-off's `pc+0xc44` is written only from `stns` (`+0x448`), which only 11 monster stun attacks
  carry (MEASURED). The approach walk (`MoveTowardObject`) refuses on `pc+0xc44` only. The 11
  byte compares with 0x11 in the server's asm sit in item-use checks, inventory and storage
  operation code and the skill gate -- none in movement.
- Client (a fork's dig, READ): the move gates are the body-state mask `FUN_009eb140` (`& 0x2476`),
  a 500 ms lock after a send, and the modal checks. No wall sets any of those bits (every setter of
  states 1, 2, 4, 6, 10, 13 listed; the cast deco's state 2 clears at its shot; the 0xB0BD buff deco
  sets none); the 0x30BF motion handler has no case for 0x11; no read of `pw` (+0x90) or `onff`
  (+0x58) on a skill ref was found in the move, attack or skill paths.
- So, per the rule "never present a guess as real", **this round does not root the caster**: a move
  with a wall up is accepted and the wall keeps absorbing (the motion leaves 0x11, as the movement
  handler's SetMotionState(WALK/RUN) does). Attacks were never refused. If the user wants the root
  anyway it is a small OURS switch -- their decision, in docs/TODO.md. It is a negative from probes,
  not a proof of absence.

**6. The client (READ).** A kind-7 entry's damage shows as an ordinary number over the caster, the
HP bar does not move, and no hit reaction plays; the wall's HP is shown nowhere. While a buff deco
naming a DefenseEfp is attached, a blow on that body plays that efp (`IDecoSkill::FUN_009cd480`, the
highest Priority) -- that it is skillaniset2's DefenseEfp column is INFERRED (+0x80 beside the
DamageEfp's +0x84): `fire_ganggi_damage_a.efp` / `hit_2_ice.efp` for the walls.

**Built.**
- Export: skill CSV columns 83..86, `pw` value[0..3] (`onff` was already in BuffParams). **The VM
  needs the skills CSV re-exported and re-imported.**
- Server: `buff` keeps the wall holder, the wall's HP, the drain clock (`HitWall`, `EndBrokenWalls`,
  `DueDrains`, `ToggleOff`); `session/walls.go` runs the drain and the broken-wall end every 100 ms
  (OURS poll), switches a running toggle off on a recast, and keeps SKILL_PROTECTIONWALL;
  `monsterStrike` sends an absorbed blow into the wall -- `resolveBlow(raw, pw[3], pw[2], crit, no
  block)`, the same pipeline -- and a broken wall ends right after the messages reporting the
  breaking blow (retail's book update: the next frame, after the blow's packet). A monster
  skill's type comes from the skill table; the counter's unnamed swing takes the monster's first
  skill whose range is its own (INFERRED: the col-83 primary); an unknown type is physical (OURS, as
  `combat.AttackType` reads 0).
- Wire (OURS): a 13-byte suffix on `OpAttackResult` and `OpMonsterAttacked`, sent only when the blow
  met a wall or the reply is a toggle-off -- every other message is byte for byte what it was.
- Client: the kind-7 drawing (number, DefenseEfp, no reaction, no HP change), the DefenseEfp on any
  monster blow on a body holding such a buff, no cast drawn for a toggle-off, the exchange line.

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-ninth round, review follow-up: the saved bar follows skill upgrades and bag moves, a death writes retail's EXP-loss line, and a held arrow turns at an aimable speed

The review confirmed round 639's READ claims. It found the following, each fixed here.

1. **The bar follows a learned skill (READ).** AddLearnedSkill `0x880be0` -> `0x778840(id, 1)` ->
   CNIFUnderMenuBar `0x60c230`:
   - It finds the new record's previous level (level byte +0x60 less one; `0x93f770(group, level)`).
   - Every skill slot (kind 0x49) holding that level's id takes the new id and icon, and is saved.
   - A level-1 skill changes nothing.

   The withdrawal `0x880db0` passes the id it names, which is the group's skill after the
   withdrawal, with 0. Slots holding exactly that id are cleared; the group's other slots take it.
   - Built as `HotbarStore.rebind_for_skill`. It runs on every successful learn: the learn result
     names no skill, so NetClient queues the requested ids and emits `learn_skill_done(id, ok)`.
   - This server has no withdrawal, so that half is built and tested but reached by nothing (OPEN).
   - Reproduced before the fix: skill 90 upgraded to 1101 still cast 90, even after a relog.
2. **The bar follows a bag move (READ).** `0x60c430` re-binds the item slots bound to a bag slot, by
   the item's ref id through the whole bag or at that slot. It is called from the item results at
   `0x87b613`, `0x88bd53` and `0x88c20b`. Ours re-resolved only on bag lists; it now also does so
   on every move answer (`_on_inventory_move_for_hotbar`) and saves.
3. **A death writes UIIT_MSG_STATE_LOSE_EXP (READ).** The line is "[N]Experience Points lost.",
   type 1, as `0x8a9b76..0x8a9baa` writes it, instead of our "You were killed. Lost N experience.".
   The revive prompt and the status label keep ours.
4. **The saved file is robust (OURS).**
   - Every field is type-checked on load; a bad entry is skipped and the rest load. Before, a
     non-integer field aborted the decode with a script error.
   - A file that exists but does not load is never written over, so no other character's entry is
     lost.
   - The write goes to `quickslots.cfg.tmp`, which is then renamed over the old file.
5. **The reload flag (READ).** In `0x8a7c50`, a flag other than 7 discards the list
   (`0x8a7ce7..0x8a7d08`), so the bar starts empty. This is recorded in the doc.
6. **The held arrow (OURS).** A click still turns 36 degrees. A held arrow repeats after retail's
   1000 ms and then every **250 ms**, which is **144 degrees a second**. Retail's 50 ms made 720
   degrees a second.
7. **Smaller fixes.**
   - The party-leave line is UIIT_MSG_PARTY_SECEDE, "[%s] has left the party.", with the name
     from the party list the client now keeps. Ours remains only for an unknown id.
   - The EXP a result reports is what was actually added (`session.expAdded`: the levels passed
     plus the progress). At the cap it is only what fitted, and 0 (no line) once full. What
     retail's server sends at the cap was not read (OPEN).
   - The window's mouse: CGWndBase's mouse slot (`0xb91440`) keeps a message inside the window's
     rect (`0xb8f3d0`, a rect test, not an art test). The whole-rect STOP matches. INFERRED: the
     window's own handler reports it handled.

**MEASURED, real X input on the box** (Login route, the round's rebuilt server in memory).
- Skill 90 was put on slot 1 by a click and on slot 4 by a drag. A real click on its ADD learned
  level 2, and both slots became 1101 and were saved.
- The potion was put on slot 7 from bag slot 0. A real drag moved it to bag slot 10, and the log
  showed "quickslot 7 follows item 4 from bag slot 0 to 10" and a save. Key 7 then "uses item 4 at
  bag slot 10" (snd_potion).
- After Escape, Restart, the bar restored {1: 1101, 4: 1101, 7: item 4 at 10}. Key 1 "casts skill
  1101" (CAST send: skill 1101), and key 7 used the potion again.
- Holding the right arrow for 2077 ms turned the doll 0.6283 -> 3.7699 rad: the press, then repeats
  at 1000, 1250, 1500, 1750 and 2000 ms, six steps of 36 degrees.

**Tests.**
- `hotbar_store_test.gd`: bad field types, no overwrite after a failed load, no leftover temp
  file, and learn/withdraw rebinds.
- `inventory_pages_test.gd`: the 250 ms repeat.
- `hud_system_message_test.gd`: the loss line.
- Go: `TestExpAddedCountsLevelsAndTheCap`.

The negative, against af79fe9 (round 639 before this follow-up):

    FAIL World3D.exp_loss_line writes retail's EXP-loss line
    SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid call. Nonexistent 'int' constructor.
    SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid get index 'skills' (on base: 'Dictionary').
    FAIL no repeat 50 ms later (retail's period is not used)
    FAIL the next repeat 250 ms after the first

  - The level-up line is not a system line: it goes to `GDR_WARNING_WND` (`0x77b580`, child 0x23,
    a CIFNotify), formatted by swprintf, so "level [40]." keeps its brackets. Ours dropped them.
- **Built.** `HudSystemMessage` implements all of the above; World3D anchors it bottom-right at
  those offsets. `_log_system(text, type)` writes there, not to the chat; HudChat's refusals go
  through `system_sink`. The level-up line shows on a second HudNotice for GDR_WARNING_WND, and
  the gold pickup reads "[N]gold gained." (retail's string; the old line was ours).
- **EXP after a kill.** The server appends `ExpGained` and `SkillExpGained` (two s64s) to
  OpAttackResult after the targetType byte; the carrier is OURS, since retail has its own EXP
  packet. The client writes retail's two lines from them, type 1. Skill EXP is `combat.go`'s
  disclosed M = 1.
- **Our own lines.** "Assigned skill to quickslot N ..." and "Put the item on quickslot N." are
  removed from the screen and go to the log: the live bar (`0x60a000..0x60efff`) calls none of the
  adds. The rest of ours stay in the window with type 0; the doc lists them.
- **Not built (OPEN).** The filter board and `chop.dat` (the button only logs), the frame's
  hover-only option (`0x4f9d00`+7), GDR_WARNING_WND's own y, guide lines and unique notices (our
  server sends neither).

**2. The hotbar is saved (READ: retail saves it on the server; ours is client-side, OURS).**

- **Retail.** CNIFUnderMenuBar `0x60bea0` sends 0x7158 on every change: slot 0..50, kind, and a u32
  (the skill id, or the item's bag slot, `0x666800`). The character-data handler `0x8ab0e0` reads
  them back through `0x8a7c50`: u8 flag, u8 count, count x {u8 slot, u8 kind, u32}; `0x60b260`
  fills the bar from them.
- **Ours.** At the user's request, `HotbarStore` keeps every skill slot (id, Basic_Code) and item
  slot (item id, bag slot) on every page, one entry per server:port and character, in
  `user://quickslots.cfg`. It is written on every change and read once the bar exists.
- **Items.** An item is re-resolved against the bag: its slot first, as retail binds it, then the
  same item anywhere.

**3. The preview's step (OURS, the user's request).** 36 degrees per arrow command instead of
retail's frame_ms * 0.0015 rad. A held arrow repeats the step at retail's 1000/50 ms, which is 720
degrees a second once repeating. The yaw wraps in [0, 360), and the reset still sets 0.

**MEASURED, real X input on the box** (Login route, the round's server in memory, 1280x720, display

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-eighth round, review follow-up: a player's premium shows on their target row, the server starts it from the item, and a target that is gone closes the window

The review of round 638 upheld every READ claim except one: **the premium does show on a
target.** The first icon of the user's retail target row is `icon\item\etc\mall_pre_apru_4w.ddj`
(correlation 0.978, the reviewer's measurement). This follow-up corrects that, makes the server
start the premium's buff, and mirrors the target window's per-frame check. Labels: READ,
MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Record: `docs/protocol/target_window_buffs.md`.

**1. The premium is a skill buff (READ, SR_GameServer.exe; MEASURED, the box's data).**
- The premium items carry `[USU1:SKILL_MALL_PRE_APRU_4W_01]` or `…_GLOBAL_4W_01`: skilldata 5412,
  29723 and 46405, `SN_SKILL_MALL_PRE_APRU_4W` / `…_GLOBAL_4W`, icon `item\etc\mall_pre_apru_4w.ddj`.
  Examples: `ITEM_MALL_PREMIUM_GOLDTIME` 9277 and `ITEM_MALL_PREMIUM_GLOBAL_SILVERTIME` 22925.
- USU1 in `GObjPC::FUN_0049f590` (0x49fad0):
  - It queues a type-0 timed job keyed by the skill id, lasting 'dura' / 1000 s. The division is
    unsigned (`mul 0x10624dd3; shr 6`): the 4-week rows hold 2,419,200,000 ms as −1875767296.
  - The manager's switch (0x6565f0, table 0x656690) makes type 0 a **CTJ_SkillKeeper**.
  - Its slot 12 (0x650e70), run as the factory 0x655be0 makes it, calls RegisterSkillInBook,
    EngageSkill and **Skill_BroadcastBuffAdded_B0BD**.
- The pre-check (0x49f4ab..0x49f4ef):
  - the skill by code (0x495690);
  - 0x1894 if the same skill's type-0 job runs (FUN_00411560(0, id));
  - 0x650d40: no 'dura' is 0x3003, then the skill gate 0x58d8f0.
- So the premium reaches every client as 0xB0BD and sits in its owner's buff list like any buff.
  Only the item-time kinds 3/4/5 (the UIL1/UIU1 grants) never reach the viewer.
- The four wrong statements are corrected: target_window_buffs.md, the round 638 entry's §3, the
  viewer's header, and the round's commit note repeated there.

**2. The server starts it (built; `session/composite.go`).**
- A composite item's USU1 entry resolves its skill by code (new `GetSkillByCode`, the lowest id,
  as items are). It refuses with 0x1894's text while the same skill's buff runs, and refuses a skill
  with no 'dura'. After the spend, it starts the buff on the user's own book (`startUsu1Buff`, under
  the owner's buff lock) for 'dura' read unsigned / 1000 s, and tells the zone with OpBuffStart.
- **OURS, changed from round 632:** an entry srrevamp does not model is now skipped and logged
  instead of refusing the whole item. These are a UIU1 3/3/13/4 (the premium time, a
  CTJ_PremiumKeeper type-3 job), a UIU1 3/3/3/10 with a FourCC other than 0x706874, BCS1, BFI1,
  PSU1, UQL1 and USL1. An item with nothing modelled is still refused and not spent.
- Not modelled: the skill gate 0x58d8f0; the buff's params (dru, odar, hr, luck, alcu, inti, stri),
  since the book models only run speed; the premium time, BFI1 and UQL1.

**3. A skill name in the second text file (READ/MEASURED).**
- `SN_SKILL_MALL_PRE_APRU_4W` ("Premium") is only in `textdata_object.txt`, not
  `textdata_equip&skill.txt` (MEASURED on the box's Media.pk2).
