## Six-hundred-and-twenty-first round, review follow-up: the trails rebuild about five times faster, only when something moved, and draw one-sided where their node says so; the texture and dedupe readings corrected

This merges round 620's review follow-up (2246d91), then fixes what the review of round 621 found.

**Merged.** Round 620's API changes are adopted:
- the link variants are skipped by command family (`EfpSim.kind_names_link`) in the compiled
  `[kind, space, payload]` schedule;
- the link origin is honoured in its new `_set_pos`, SetSpherePos and Attraction;
- a refused spawn under the new caps (`can_spawn`) is never linked, and every death still
  unlinks through `_on_death`.
- `clear()` now also breaks every link/next_link pair and emitter tail. Particle is RefCounted,
  so a chain left linked would have kept itself alive.

**Corrections (READ):**
- **The dedupe.**
  - LinkDPipe (0x00c8df3f–0x00c8dfdd) and LinkPipe write each particle into the next free slot
    and advance only when it is taken. So a near-duplicate is **dropped** and the older point
    kept.
  - Only LinkObj advances first and overwrites the last pair, and it keeps comparing against the
    position it took (local_48).
  - Round 621 had "overwrites" for all three.
  - The retail quirk is noted: LinkPipe compares its first particle against uninitialised
    local_58, because its counter starts at 1. This client takes the first particle (OURS).
- **The DDJ loader.** The runtime path is `FUN_00b88420` → `FUN_00b87f20` ("DDJCreateTextureHForMThread
  Error - %s").
  - It opens exactly the path it is handed through the archive object's vtable +0x2c, checks
    "JMXV", and passes the buffer from offset 20 (size field − 8) to D3DX with the file's own
    MipLevels.
  - Round 621 cited `FUN_00b8eb60`, a converter path the game does not run.
  - "No path rewrite", and so `water_offset_01`'s unreachability, are re-derived from
    `FUN_00b88420`. That the archive handed in is Particles.pk2's is INFERRED.
- **The billboard matrix.** `0x00edbde8` is now READ as the inverse view's right, up and look
  rows (round 620's follow-up, `CEFSystem::FUN_00cb0ee0`). The pipe's side is right·d.y − up·d.x.
- **The +0x34 case list is complete.** There are 28 cases, all listed from the decompile:
  0x03, 0x08, 0x0d, 0x12, 0x15, 0x18, 0x1b–0x1e, 0x21, 0x24, 0x27–0x2a, 0x2d, 0x30,
  0x33–0x36, 0x39, 0x3d, 0x41, 0x45, 0x49, 0x4b. They are exactly `names_link`'s set.
- **Follow** (new; EFP_FORMAT.md "Follow"):
  - The body's 20-byte block lands at node +0x154..+0x16c (`FUN_00cc3500`).
  - `CEFGroup::vslot_004` turns its u32s into ancestors, N levels up: u2 position, u3 rotation
    (a negative value sets emitter +0x74), u4 velocity, u6 spawn-relative.
  - `CEFUpdater::vslot_002` applies a follow only on a frame when that ancestor's +0x60
    "transform changed" flag is set.
  - This client now lets a node with u2 = 0 not follow its parent (READ). Every other node keeps
    round 620's parent-translation follow (OURS).

**MEASURED:**
- **The q textures.** Only the top level is clean. Level 1 of `_q_2` holds 15 non-zero values down
  to −512, and every other stored mip of all four files is zero. Round 621's "every channel in
  0..1" held for the top level only.
  - This client keeps clean Godot-built mips (OURS, not retail's look when minified).
  - It now rounds f16 to 8 bits: 0.5 gives 128, where round 621 truncated to 127.
- **The follow levels over the 95,801 retail nodes:**
  - u2 = 0: 22,762;
  - 1 ≤ u2 ≤ depth: 69,695;
  - u2 = depth + 1: 3,344.
- **The census** now builds the Link strips at all 40 frames and keeps each file's peak
  one-frame triangle count. Round 621 summed one frame.
  - 975 files draw a Link node. **417** of them make a Link triangle at some frame.
  - Per effect, the one-frame peak has median 141, 90th percentile 492, max 1,392.
  - "Draw every node" is unchanged at **4,013 (96.2 %)**, and there are 0 script errors.
- **Why 510 Link files make no strip** (INFERRED cause):
  - Every chain sits at one point through 40 frames. The examples (`battle\hwan_g/_v/_y`,
    `battle\deco_wind_jumpkick_a`, `cos\p2skill_ass_dinosaur_attack5`) are u2 = 0 Link nodes
    with no position command, under a still root.
  - Their trail can only come from the effect moving through the world, and this client
    simulates in the effect's local space (round 620, OURS).
  - This is the next lever (OPEN, in TODO.md).

**Performance** (the reviewer's bench `rv621r/link_bench.gd`, headless on the box, raw
`_update_links` cost per call):
- Two changes to run it:
  - the triangle count reads the strip, since the mesh is no longer an ImmediateMesh;
  - each call refills the new per-frame budget, since the bench rebuilds hundreds of times in
    one frame.
- The copy is `efplink_bench.gd` in the lane's scratch.

| effect × instances | round 621 | follow-up | faster |
|---|---|---|---|
| cold_ganggi_keep_f × 1 | 3.18 ms | 0.58 ms | 5.5× |
| cold_ganggi_keep_f × 10 | 21.44 | 4.50 | 4.8× |
| help_ganggi_keep_a × 1 | 3.05 | 0.58 | 5.3× |
| help_ganggi_keep_a × 10 | 21.55 | 4.55 | 4.7× |
| cleric_resurrection_monser_keep_b × 1 | 1.00 | 0.20 | 5.0× |
| cleric_resurrection_monser_keep_b × 10 | 10.11 | 2.02 | 5.0× |
| cleric_resurrection_monser_keep_b × 40 | 18.49 | 4.38 | 4.2× |
| lightning_storm_shoot_c × 1 | 0.61 | 0.15 | 4.1× |
| lightning_storm_shoot_c × 10 | 6.69 | 1.51 | 4.4× |
| lightning_storm_shoot_c × 40 | 12.64 | 4.41 | 2.9× |

- The raw build is 2.9–5.5× faster: the 5× target is met on the single-aura rows and missed on
  the crowded ones.
- On top of that, a strip is now rebuilt only after a simulation step (20 Hz), or, for a pipe,
  when the camera or the effect moved. Round 621 rebuilt it every rendered frame. So on a still
  camera at 60 fps, a `cold_ganggi_keep_f` aura costs about 12 ms a second instead of 191.
- The rows for 40 ganggi auras show 0 triangles in both columns: the particle cap leaves them
  none. They measure overhead only.

What changed (OURS):
- The geometry is built in reused packed buffers (`EfpLinks.Buf`, `Out`), with no per-point
  objects and no per-sample arrays. Each chain is walked from its head along next_link while
  gathering.
- Each node's chains are stitched into one PRIMITIVE_TRIANGLE_STRIP ArrayMesh with degenerate
  joins and no index buffer.
- The colour lerp is inlined with the same fistp rounding.
- A budget, `LINK_TRIS_PER_FRAME` = 20,000 triangles per rendered frame across all effects, caps
  the rebuild. A node past it keeps last frame's strips.

**Other fixes:**
- **The Link shader** is a real template variant: `{UVMAP}` holds the instance UV line for plates
  and meshes and nothing for strips. Round 621 used a string replace.
- **Cull.** A Link strip takes its node's cull (+0x1a4). The reviewer measured 17 LinkObj and 4
  LinkPipe nodes with cull 3.
  - The triangles are emitted with the orientation reversed against D3D's, the BmsReader
    convention (INFERRED).
  - Each stitched chain starts at an odd strip position so its triangles keep that orientation.

**Tests.**
- **`efp_links_test.gd`** was reworked for the packed API and grew. It now also covers:
  - drop versus overwrite in the dedupe;
  - D3D's strip triangles, each reversed;
  - two chains in one strip that are never joined by a drawn triangle and keep one orientation;
  - chains staying consistent past a refused spawn and a dead head;
  - `clear()` breaking the link pairs;
  - u2 = 0 against u2 = 1 follow;
  - the Link shader without, and the plate shader with, the INSTANCE_CUSTOM line;
  - the cull honoured;
  - no rebuild without a step;
  - the budget keeping last frame's strips.
- **`ddj_reader_test.gd`**: 0.5 rounds to 128.
- **Results:**
  - `remote_godot.sh check`: ALL LOAD.
  - `remote_godot.sh tests`: 136 suites, 0 failing.
  - `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...`: ok.

Against round 621's merge (a648c36), the new tests fail:

```
SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid get index 'Buf' (on base: 'GDScript').
SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid get index 'Out' (on base: 'GDScript').
FAIL clear() breaks every link pair (no RefCounted cycle is left)
SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid call. Nonexistent function 'surface_get_primitive_type' in base 'ImmediateMesh'.
FAILURES: 1
FAIL A16B16G16R16F: 0.5 rounds to 128, not 127 (got 127)
```

- the ancestor-level follow and its +0x60 gate;
- the rotation and velocity follows;

## Six-hundred-and-twenty-first round: the particle trails draw -- ribbons, lightning and streamers -- and 96 % of the effects now draw every node they mean to

The user asked for "most of the particles loaded". After round 620, 3,062 of 4,170 effect files
(73.4 %) drew every node they meant to draw. The gaps were:
- the three Link render modes: RenderLinkPipe (864 files), RenderLinkObj (128) and
  RenderLinkDPipe (70);
- textures that do not load (68);
- meshes that do not load (16).

This round reads the three Link routines and draws them. It also reads the particle "link"
that round 620 took to be the parent, decodes the DDJ "q" format, and establishes why every
remaining asset fails. `docs/protocol/EFP_FORMAT.md` "Link render modes" and "Assets that do not
load" carry the addresses.

**READ** (sro_client.exe, `/var/tmp/decomp_client` and `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm` on the box):
- **The link is the emitter's previous live particle, not the parent.**
  - The emitter constructor `FUN_00c88320` puts a particle list at emitter +0x30, with prev
    offset 0x34 and next offset 0x38.
  - The particle init `FUN_00c88490` (particle vtable 0x00e0ebfc, slot 4) appends each new
    particle at the tail (the call at 0x00c88769). A death (`FUN_00c87a20`) unlinks it
    (`FUN_00c873a0`).
  - So particle +0x34 is the particle the same emitter spawned before it that is still alive.
  - Every link variant of the per-particle program tests +0x34 first and does nothing without
    one: cases 0x03, 0x08, 0x0d, 0x12, 0x15, 0x18, 0x1b–0x1e, 0x21, 0x28, 0x2d, 0x36, 0x39,
    0x3d, 0x41, 0x45, 0x49 and 0x4b.
  - `EfpSim` now keeps that list (`Particle.link`, `next_link`) and skips those variants
    (`EfpSim.names_link`).
- **One strip per emitter.** Each Link routine returns unless +0x34 is 0. The oldest live particle
  walks the list to the newest.
  - A point is (position, colour, scale.x as the width).
  - A point closer than 1e-6 on every axis (`0x00e1b848`) to the last one taken replaces it.
- **LinkDPipe** (`FUN_00c8de80`) passes the points straight to the ribbon. Retail's lightning
  files place those particles with SetSpherePos, so the line is jagged.
- **LinkPipe** (`FUN_00c8e020`) runs a uniform cubic B-spline through the points, with both ends
  doubled.
  - It takes 3 samples per segment at t = 0, 1/3, 2/3. The weights come from the doubles 3, 6, 4
    and 1 at `0x00e1b808`, `0x00d99a68`, `0x00e1b860` and `0x00e1b7f0`.
  - Colour is lerped byte by byte and rounded; the width steps linearly.
  - So m points give 3(m − 1) + 1.
- **The ribbon** (`FUN_00c8d0e0`):
  - Each point is projected to NDC. The call has the shape of `D3DXVec3Project(out, v, NULL,
    proj 0x00edbea8, view 0x00edbe68, NULL)` (INFERRED).
  - The screen direction is taken by central difference; the ends use their one neighbour.
  - (d.y, −d.x, 0) is turned by the billboard matrix `0x00edbde8` and normalised.
  - The vertices are P ± n·width, with v = 0 and 1, and u = i/(N − 1).
  - It is drawn as D3DPT_TRIANGLESTRIP (5, pushed at 0x00c8d0c1) and flushed per strip.
- **LinkObj** (`FUN_00c8c3a0`):
  - Its edges are pos ± scale.x × the particle's own rotation Y row (+0xc0).
  - The same B-spline runs over the pairs with the first pair doubled. Only k − 2 segments are
    sampled, so the newest particle is a control point only.
  - u runs from 1 to 0 in steps of 2.0 (`0x00e1b898`) over the sample-vertex count.
- **Texture.** `CEFCShape::FUN_00c883d0` gives each particle its node's first mesh entry and
  that entry's first texture. `FUN_00cabda0` binds it for every render mode, Links included.
  This makes round 620's OURS "first mesh entry, first texture" a READ.
- **The DDJ loader** (`FUN_00b8eb60`) checks "JMXV", skips 20 bytes, and hands the DDS to the
  statically linked D3DX (`D3DXGetImageInfoFromFileInMemory`, then
  `D3DXCreateTextureFromFileInMemoryEx`). It applies no path rewrite.
- **`JMXVBMS 0109` is refused by the retail client too.**
  - Both .bms header checks accept only `0110`: `Prim::FUN_00bc5690` (case 1, Prim.cpp line
    0xd9) and `PrimGeometry::FUN_00c121f0` (PrimGeometry.cpp line 0x152). A mismatch asserts,
    then the load returns 0.
  - The binary's only 0109 branch (`ResObject::FUN_00bce3b0`) is the `.bsr` header.
  - So there is no 0109 mesh layout to add to the .bms reader, and none was added.

**MEASURED** (the box's retail archives):
- **The "q" textures are D3DFMT_A16B16G16R16F.** The DDS FourCC slot holds `71 00 00 00`,
  D3DFORMAT 113.
  - The four files (`textures\ques1_monster_paper_q_2..5.ddj`) are 128×128 with 8 mips, and
    every channel is in 0..1.
  - Each payload is twice its 174,760-byte chain. Only the top level is read.
  - `DdjReader` now decodes them.
- **Every remaining asset failure**, from the new `efp_census.gd --build --assets`, which checks
  Particles.pk2, Media.pk2 and Data.pk2, other extensions, and the basename in any folder:
  - 20 texture paths are absent everywhere.
  - 4 exist only at another path: `water_offset_01.ddj` only as Data.pk2
    `Prim\Mtrl\etc\...`, which the loader cannot reach, and `eu_harp_13`, `eu_shield_13` and
    `eu_sword_13` only as meshes.
  - In 36 files a drawn node has no texture entry, and in 10 an empty texture name.
  - Meshes: the two 0109 files above, and 4 paths absent everywhere.
  - The 4 q-texture files also name an absent `-glow` texture, so decoding them changes no
    file-level count.
- **Link chains are the size of their effects.** In `cold_ganggi_keep_f`, twelve LinkPipe nodes
  make 6–7-particle chains 5–12 units long and 0.2–0.6 wide. The seven lightning DPipe chains of
  `lightning_storm_shoot_c` hold up to 13 points over about 10 units.
- **The build census**, `efp_census.gd --build`, 88 s:

  | | round 620 | round 621 |
  |---|---|---|
  | draw every node they mean to draw | 3,062 (73.4 %) | **4,013 (96.2 %)** |
  | draw at least one node | 3,985 (95.6 %) | 4,100 (98.3 %) |
  | files skipping a node for a texture | 68 | 75 |
  | files skipping a node for a mesh | 16 | 16 |
  | Link nodes skipped | 1,062 files | 0 |

  - The census now also builds each Link strip at frame 40: 27,212 triangles across the archive,
    with 0 script errors.
  - Files skipping a node for a texture rose from 68 to 75 because Link nodes now reach their
    texture check. The 7 new ones are Link nodes with an empty texture name (3 files),
    `crash_glow.ddj` (3) and `oura_0555.ddj` (1), all absent.

**INFERRED:**
- that `thunk_FUN_00aa30f0` is D3DXVec3Project, from its six-argument shape through D3DX's
  dispatch table at `0x00ec7758`;
- that `0x00edbde8` holds the camera's right and up rows (round 620's billboard inference, used
  the same way here);
- that D3DX ignores the surplus q payload;
- that a node whose mesh fails to load draws nothing in retail.

**OURS:**
- Link strips are drawn two-sided, as triangle lists.
- Without a camera, the projection is orthographic down −Z of the effect's axes.
- The q textures are converted to RGBA8, top level only.
- Nodes with no texture stay undrawn (see OPEN).

**Tests.**
- **`efp_links_test.gd`** (new, synthetic, 52 checks). It covers:
  - the B-spline weights;
  - fistp rounding and the per-byte colour lerp;
  - the 1e-6 dedupe;
  - strip-to-triangle winding;
  - DPipe ribbon offsets, UVs and colours on a line seen head-on;
  - LinkPipe sample counts, the first sample, width steps, the colour at t = 1/3, and a straight
    chain staying straight;
  - LinkObj's 2-particle no-draw, 8-vertex strip, closing pair, u from 1 to 0, and the width
    following the particle's own Y axis;
  - the emitter chain, including unlinking on death;
  - SetPosition space 2 with and without a link;
  - EfpEffect drawing each Link mode into one ImmediateMesh surface of whole triangles;
  - a Link node without a texture being reported.

## Six-hundred-and-twentieth round, review follow-up: effects follow the game's own cast phases, end when their buff or cast ends, and survive an equipment change

The review of round 620 checked its READ claims against the asm and found real defects. This follow-up fixes them.

**READ** (sro_client.exe, box decompile and asm):
- **The cast's phase machine** (IDecoSkill, funcs_015):
  - A cast (`GlobalDataManager::FUN_00a53610`) enters phase 0 through `FUN_00a534d0`.
  - Each phase plays its clip, advances +0xbe, and fires its StartEvent 0 rows at once
    (`FUN_00a53480` → `FUN_00a52fe0`).
  - Each animation event of the current clip fires the next StartEvent (`FUN_00a59970`, type 1).
    The clip's end (type 100) moves on: READY → WAIT → SHOT.
  - A phase with no clip of its own advances at once. This is the skill record's per-phase clip
    count at +8 + phase.
  - WAIT holds only while the skill has WAIT clips, until the server's skill-action message
    (`FUN_00a56680` kind 1 → `FUN_00a53090`) forces SHOT.
  - ACT_S and ACT_L fire when the skill acts (`FUN_00a53850`).
- **Ending a kept effect.** It ends through the interface's slot 2 (`CEFEffect::vslot_002`), which
  frees its particles at once, or through slot 4 with 0 (`vslot_004`), which clears the restart
  flag +0x49 and releases the effect at keep count 0.
  - Slot 4 with 1 is AT_LOOP's restart (`vslot_000` resets the ages).
  - So `EfpEffect.stop()` now drops every particle at once. Round 620 let a looping effect finish
    its cycle, which never ended the 18 loop and never-extinct files the review found (among them
    `status_bad_temptation` and `pet2_dragon_j`).
- **Frame scheduling** is a single-precision running sum of the step, truncated. Key i runs at
  `ftol(f_i)`, where `f_{i+1} = f32(f_i + step)`, while `f_i ≤ end` (the loop at `0x00ca9276`, the
  fldcw at `0x00ca92b0`).
- **NeverExtinct with N = 0** kills the particle (`FUN_00c84d80`).
- **SetSpherePos space 0** (`0x00c8a4c5`):
  - The ball point is written straight into the position.
  - Then `position += value × V`. V is a stack vector the case never sets. It holds what an earlier
    command of the same frame's run left there: the o = 0 cone positions, ConeForce, Attraction or
    SetSpherePos itself.
  - With nothing earlier, V is uninitialised. EfpSim keeps V per particle run and starts it at zero,
    which is OURS for that case. 66 retail commands use space 0.
- **ConeForce space 0** falls through into 0x47 (`0x00c8ac1d` → `0x00c8ac23`), so it adds a second
  cone rotated by the particle's own rotation (121 commands).
- **Round 620's INFERRED claims the review confirmed:**
  - Force adds to the velocity (`0x00c8aae8`).
  - TextureSlide stores the UV rectangle (`0x00c8af77`).
  - The billboard matrices come from `CEFSystem::FUN_00cb0ee0`, as the inverse view with its
    translation zeroed. YBillboard has only its row 1 forced to (0, 1, 0), and its rows 0 and 2 are
    kept. Round 620 rebuilt YBillboard as an orthonormal upright basis, which was wrong.

**INFERRED:**
- **Billboard look direction.** The inverse view's rows are right, up and look. The client keeps
  the game's coordinates unconverted, so look is Godot's −camera.z. Round 620 used +camera.z, which
  put a billboarded mesh's depth backwards.
- **Phase timing.** With no per-phase clips, the phases are timed from skilldata: READY spans
  Action_PreparingTime (col 11) and WAIT spans Action_CastingTime (col 12).

**MEASURED:**
- **Colour.** A white texture under a 0x80 particle colour, a 0x80 texture under a white colour, and
  an unshaded StandardMaterial3D with albedo 0x80 all render 128 on the box's GL Compatibility
  renderer. The colours match D3D's fixed pipeline, so the suspected sRGB defect is not one.
- **The simulation costs about 7 µs a particle-frame in GDScript.** `water_assist_motion_wait`
  took 466 µs for 64 particles. The review's bench (20 copies of each file):

  | file | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | `cos\p2skill_critical_defense.efp` | 12 ms for 2,092 particles | 10.4 ms for 1,292 (capped) |
  | `cold_gigongta_keep_a.efp` | | 3.5 ms for 160 |

  Precompiling each command's key value out of the per-particle loop and dropping finished emitters
  gained about 5–10 %. The rest is GDScript per-particle work.

**What changed:**
1. **Phase timing.** `SkillEffects.cast(skill, caster, target, timings)` is the cast sequencer:
   - READY at once;
   - WAIT at prep;
   - SHOT at once when the skill has no WAIT row, else at `shot(caster)` (the server's answer) or
     at prep + cast (the OURS fallback);
   - the cast's READY/WAIT loops end when SHOT starts;
   - `hit(caster, target, skill)` fires SHOT/1 and later, and `act(skill, caster, target,
     with_aura)` fires ACT_S (plus one ACT_L cycle);
   - `cancel_cast(caster)` ends a refused or interrupted cast.

   `play_phase` no longer stops READY loops on any later phase. World3D's monster cast now uses the
   sequencer: `cast` at the request, `hit` and `act` when the blow lands, and `cancel_cast` on a
   refusal. The target is the monster the request names, where round 620 used the stale
   `_last_attack_target`. The self-cast wiring is left to the int/skills merge.
2. **Ending effects.** `stop()` ends at once. An aura also ends by itself `AURA_GRACE_MS` (2 s,
   OURS) after its buff's remaining time, in case OpBuffEnd never arrives.
3. **Equipment changes.** An effect is now a child of the body, not of its skeleton. Each frame it
   takes the frame of the body's current skeleton at its bone (`EfpEffect.follow_host`).
   - An equipment change no longer frees the auras.
   - An aura attached before the skeleton exists finds it when the skeleton arrives.
   - `skeleton_of` skips skeletons queued for deletion.
4. **Cap priority** (OURS):
   - 2,000 particles in all, of which 600 are reserved for the local player's own effects
     (`reserved`: its casts, hits and level-up); everyone else's stop at 1,400;
   - a MultiMesh is rewritten only after a simulation frame, or when the camera turns for a
     billboarded node.
5. **Hitches and caches.**
   - A skill's effect files decode on a WorkerThreadPool task when the skill state arrives (known
     skills) and on a hotbar assignment (`SkillEffects.preload_skill`, `EfpEffect.preload_paths`).
     The task produces plain data, and the resources are made on first use.
   - The caches are bounded by least-recent use, OURS: templates 256, textures 384, meshes 256. An
     evicted texture takes its materials with it.
6. **Smaller fixes.**
   - Casts and auras of freed bodies are pruned in `process()`.
   - The world's `_exit_tree` clears every live effect and the own-body reference (`clear_live`),
     which covers leave and relog.
   - An effect that draws nothing is freed rather than orphaned, in `play_phase`, `attach_aura`,
     the hit and the level-up.
   - The QA cast hook drives the sequencer.

**API changes** (for round 621's merge):
- *Behaviour:*
  - `EfpEffect.stop()` now ends at once;
  - `SkillEffects.play_phase` no longer stops phase loops;
  - `SkillEffects.attach` parents to the body and uses `follow_host`.
- *Removed:* `EfpEffect.follow(skel, bone, offset)`, replaced by `follow_host(host, bone_name,
  offset)`; `SkillEffects.stop_phase_loops`.
- *New in SkillEffects:* `cast`, `shot`, `hit`, `act`, `cancel_cast`, `cast_phase`, `process`, `tick`,
  `preload_skill`, `preload_skills`, `paths_for`, `parse_timings`, `clear_live`, `tracked_count`
  and `own_body`.
- *Extended in SkillEffects:* `attach_aura(..., remaining_ms, now_ms)` and
  `set_rows(rows, timings)`.
- *New in EfpEffect:* `reserved`, `draw_updates`, `preload_paths`, `wait_preloads`, `cache_sizes`
  and `CACHE_*`.
- *New in EfpSim:* `reserved`, `RESERVE`, `key_frames`, `can_spawn`; `MAX_TOTAL` is now 2000.
- *World3D:* `_audio_cast_start(skill_id, monster_id)`. `combat_audio_test.gd`'s source probe
  follows it.

**Tests.**
- **`efp_sim_test.gd`** adds:
  - the immediate stop of loop and never-extinct effects;
  - draws rewritten only on a stepped frame;
  - the billboard rows, and YBillboard's forced row 1;
  - NeverExtinct N = 0;
  - the float32 schedule (step 0.3 → frames 0,0,0,0,1,1,1);
  - SetSpherePos space 0, with and without a preceding cone;
  - ConeForce space 0 adding twice;
  - the reserved share.
- **`skill_effects_test.gd`** (now run on the first frame, so the tree is live) adds:
  - an effect as the body's child at the bone;
  - a skeleton rebuilt under an aura, and a queued skeleton being skipped;
  - an aura attached before the skeleton exists;
  - the sequencer: READY holding for prep, WAIT holding, `shot`, the prep + cast fallback, prep 0
    with no WAIT, and `hit` on the struck body;
  - `cancel_cast`, and `act` with and without the aura cycle;
  - a nothing-drawing effect freed;
  - aura replacement, detach and detach_owner;
  - the aura's grace expiry, freed-body pruning, and the bounded template cache.
- **Results.**
  - `remote_godot.sh check`: ALL LOAD.
  - `remote_godot.sh tests`: 135 suites, 0 failing.
  - `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...`: ok. The server is unchanged.
- Against round 620 (41163cb), the new checks fail: see below.

## Six-hundred-and-twentieth round: skills play their own particle effects -- the cast glow, the imbue's hand aura, the heal's burst -- drawn from the game's own .efp files

The user asked for skill visual effects on activation, and for "most of the particles loaded in".
Round 619 decoded the files. This round plays them:
- `EfpSim` (`client/scripts/efp/efp_sim.gd`) runs the client's own particle rules over the decoded
  tree.
- `EfpEffect` (`efp_effect.gd`) draws them as one MultiMesh per node, under the Compatibility
  renderer.
- `SkillEffects` (`client/scripts/effects/skill_effects.gd`) plays each skilleffectset row's
  `.efp` at the moments SkillAudio plays the same row's sound. It keeps the ACT_L auras per buff
  token.

The rules are written down, with addresses, in `docs/protocol/EFP_FORMAT.md` "Playback".

**READ** (sro_client.exe, `/var/tmp/decomp_client` and `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm` on the box):
- **A frame is 50 ms.** `UI_ALCHEMYBOX::FUN_00bc1490` accumulates the game's millisecond delta
  (`DAT_0110f7f8`) and hands `ftol(acc / 50.0)` frames to every effect. The double 50.0 is at
  `0x00d8f0b0`.
  - The frames travel `CRTModParticle::FUN_00c80ff0` → `CEFEffect::vslot_000` → interface +0x4c,
    which is effect +0x28c. The extinct executors add that to each particle's age.
  - INFERRED: the delta is in milliseconds. The game loop caps it at 3000, beside a float twin
    capped at 3.0.
  - This closes round 619's first OPEN.
- **Spawning makes emitters.** `FUN_00c86cd0` gives each new particle one emitter per child node.
  A child node therefore emits relative to each of its parent's particles, on the parent's age.
- **The three lifetimes:**
  - NormalTimeExtinct (`FUN_00c84e20`) dies after frame N−1;
  - NormalTimeLoop (`…dd0`) wraps the age modulo N;
  - NeverExtinct (`…d80`) holds the age at 1.
- **The per-particle program is an opcode interpreter** (`EFEffect::FUN_00c893f0`, a
  0x52-case switch). Each command's factory stores `base + space`, so the `space` byte round 619
  left OPEN selects a variant:
  - for positions, `space = r×3 + o`: `o` is the origin (none, parent, link) and `r` the frame the
    value is rotated by (none, own, parent, link);
  - for velocities and forces, the rotation frame.
  - The table of bases, and every variant, is in EFP_FORMAT.md.
- **Cone vectors.** The vector is `(0, lerp(min, max, r), 0)`, turned `r·angle` about Z
  (`IDecoSkill::FUN_00a4d820`: `FUN_00b44b40` is fsin, `FUN_00b44a10` fcos), then `r·2π` about Y.
  - The sphere position is a rejection-sampled unit-ball point times the value.
  - Attraction adds the normalised offset from the parent, times the value.
- **Motion and defaults** (`CEFUpdater::vslot_002` and the particle init):
  - each frame, `pos += vel`, and the rotation and shape rotations step;
  - a new particle takes its parent's position, velocity and rotation, with scale 1, colour
    0xFFFFFFFF and UV rectangle (0,0,1,1).
- **The draw routines.** The render command's factories store `space + 1..5`, and every retail
  render command has space 0 (MEASURED). So:

  | value | mode | routine |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | Plate | `FUN_00c8c210` |
  | 2 | Mesh | `FUN_00c8bf50` |
  | 3 | LinkDPipe | `FUN_00c8de80` |
  | 4 | LinkPipe | `FUN_00c8e020` |
  | 5 | LinkObj | `FUN_00c8c3a0` |

  - A plate is the unit quad at `0x00edb070`, scaled per axis.
  - Every vertex takes the particle's colour, and UVs map as `u0 + u·du`.
  - This closes round 619's second OPEN.
- **The view modes** (`FUN_00cabda0`, the switch at `0xcabf1b`):
  - ViewNone uses the particle's rotation;
  - Billboard and YBillboard use the camera matrices at `0x00edbde8` and `0x00edbe28`. That
    these are the camera-facing and upright-facing billboards is INFERRED from the names;
  - VBillboard builds a basis with Y along the velocity.
- **ActType** (`IDecoSkill::FUN_00a51bc0`, the row's +0xe byte):
  - AT_ONE_FOLLOW (0) is created with its keep flag 0 and goes to the one-shot list;
  - AT_LOOP and AT_STOP (1, 2) are created with the keep flag 1.

**MEASURED** (the box's retail archives):
- **The skilleffectset header** names ActType, Obj Path, ObjName, StartBone and StartOffset at
  0-based 13 and 17–20. The imbue's rows are `ACT_S AT_ONE_FOLLOW cold_gigongta_motion_a.efp` and
  `ACT_L AT_LOOP cold_gigongta_keep_a.efp`, both at `Bip01 R Finger2`.
- **The "keep" auras are short one-shots.** `cold_gigongta_keep_a` is a 20-frame (1 s) root
  particle whose children emit for 20 frames, all NormalTimeExtinct. So AT_LOOP has to restart
  the file for the aura to last.
- **BSAnimation needs no drawing.** All 3,230 nodes that carry a BSAnimation variable or a BAN
  controller are RenderNone. Their motion reaches particles as the baked SetBANPos and SetBANRot
  keys.
- **AngleVector1's b.z** is a.z in radians in every retail value.
- **The build census**, new `--build` mode of `client/tools/efp_census.gd`, 86 s. It builds every
  decoded file into an EfpEffect with its real meshes and textures, and runs 2 s of it:

  | | files | % of 4,170 |
  |---|---|---|
  | built without error | 4,103 of 4,103 decoded | 98.4 |
  | draw at least one node | 3,985 | 95.6 |
  | draw every node they mean to draw | 3,062 | 73.4 |

  The skipped nodes, by files:

  | skipped | files |
  |---|---|
  | RenderLinkPipe | 864 |
  | RenderLinkObj | 128 |
  | RenderLinkDPipe | 70 |
  | a texture that does not load (4 DDJ in the unhandled "q" format, the rest missing) | 68 |
  | a mesh that does not load (2 are `JMXVBMS 0109`) | 16 |

  The 2 s of simulation spawned 279,962 particles across the archive, without a script error.

**INFERRED:**
- the cone's angle is `b.z`;
- TextureSlide's key is the UV rectangle (the decompile loses the store; the draw routines' UV
  mapping is READ);
- Force's add targets the velocity;
- SetGraphRandomScale samples the node's first BlendScaleGraph, linearly;
- a Frame* value i belongs to frame `start + i·step`.

**OURS** (listed in the code and in EFP_FORMAT.md):
- the particle "link" (+0x34) is taken to be the parent;
- following the parent is translation only;
- the order within a frame is motion, commands, emission, ages;
- the emitters of a dead particle stop;
- there is a cap of 300 particles per effect and 3,000 in all, and a refused spawn gives its 1.0
  back;
- the emission globals are at full quality;
- the Godot blend mapping:
  - SRCALPHA/ONE → ADD;
  - ONE/ONE → ADD with alpha 1;
  - SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA and BOTHSRCALPHA → MIX;
  - ZERO/INVSRCALPHA → MIX with black;

## Six-hundred-and-nineteenth round, review follow-up: four field meanings corrected, and the Go and GDScript readers proven identical value for value

The review of round 619 found the byte layouts right but four field **meanings** wrong, and places
where the two readers could disagree. All of it was re-read from the asm, and every correction is
now checked against the whole archive.

**Corrections (READ):**
- **SEFStaticEmit** (`FUN_00c84e70` c84f25–c84f68, particle death `FUN_00c87a20`).
  - The fourth field is **max_live**, the cap on live particles. The f32 is **per_trigger**,
    added to an accumulator at emitter +0x60 on each trigger. `ftol(new) − ftol(old)` particles
    spawn, and each death subtracts 1.0.
  - Two globals scale it. `DAT_01114d54` multiplies the interval. `DAT_01114d58`, when it is below
    per_trigger, halves the cap (×0.5 at 0xe1b7e0, floor 1).
  - One routine at 0x005474b1 sets both from an option read with atoi: 0 gives (0,0), 1 gives
    (2,10), anything else (5,10). Both start at 0 in `.bss`, which is full quality; the readers
    default to that, and the option's retail default is OPEN.
  - Round 619 had these as "count per burst" and "quality".
- **End mode 3** divides by the double **−100.0** at 0x00db9a38. So end = start − ftol(End/−100)·N,
  which is start + int(End/100)·N. Retail uses it (MEASURED): 9 Force commands in
  `skill_cast_foot_*.efp`, 12 SetShapeRot in `dun\bagh_masin_bronze_light.efp`, and 1,803
  StaticEmit headers. Round 619 had called it unused and guessed +100.
- **Node.ID is HeadLen.** It is the byte length of the node's name and controller block
  (MEASURED 95,801 of 95,801); the loader's cache mode seeks past that span.
  - Renamed `Node.HeadLen` / `EfpNode.head_len`, with `HeadLenMatches()` / `head_len_matches()`.
    The census counts mismatches: 0.
- **FrameBANRotation/FrameBANPosition head is an f32** (fld/fstp). It is not zero in 174 and 20
  retail commands. Round 619 had it as u32 and "0 everywhere".
- **FrameTextureSlide head** is three floats: (3,2,1) 5,378, (3,2,2) 2,646, (3,3,0.25) 990,
  (8,8,0.9) 346 occurrences. INFERRED: atlas columns, rows and a rate. The consumer was not
  traced (OPEN).

**Reader agreement (OURS where marked):**
- Timing now runs in single precision, with 32-bit integer products and the client's `_ftol`
  (0x80000000 out of range), in both readers.
  - With it, **132,666 of the 132,668 retail Frame\* parameters hold exactly their command's
    Keys**. Round 619 had 25 misses. The 2 left are `map\euro_constan_center.efp`'s TextureSlide
    (End 63 % of 40 frames = 1 key, but 26 values stored; INFERRED stale editor data).
  - Garbage headers can no longer produce huge ranges. A negative count reads as 0 (OURS).
- Strings are cut at the first NUL, like `c_str`. Bytes above 0x7f map to the same code points
  (Latin-1) in both readers; EUC-KR is not decoded (OURS).
- Graph keys are stored the client's way, as a map by time: sorted, and the last write wins.
- The magic is checked on all 8 bytes.

**New tools and gates:**
- `client/tools/efp_dump_diff.sh` diffs a canonical dump of every decoded file from each reader:
  every field, floats as bits, and each command's range and Keys. The result is **IDENTICAL**
  for all 4,103 files.
  - The first run found 10 differing files. Each was a signalling NaN in a garbage header field,
    quieted by GDScript's double; dumps now print any NaN as `nan`.
- `TestRetailCensus` now enforces:
  - at least 4,103 decoded and at least 4,096 exact;
  - zero HeadLen mismatches;
  - at most the 2 measured Frame\* key-count mismatches.

**MEASURED, the census after the follow-up:** 4,170 files; 4,103 headers parsed and 4,103
decoded; 4,096 to the exact byte; 6 zero-padded; 1 with other trailing bytes; 95,801 nodes.

**API changes that affect round 620:**

| before | after |
|---|---|
| `StaticEmit.Count` / `"count"` | `MaxLive` / `"max_live"` |
| `StaticEmit.Quality` / `"quality"` | `PerTrigger` / `"per_trigger"` |
| `Node.ID` / `EfpNode.id` | `HeadLen` / `head_len` |
| FrameBAN* `Head` / `"head"`: u32 | f32 |

New: `StaticEmit.Tick`, `EmitGlobals`, `DefaultEmitGlobals` in Go; `EfpReader.emit_tick`,
`EfpReader.ftol`, `EfpReader.f32`, `EfpReader.i32` and `EfpReader.latin1` in GDScript; and
`frame_range()["keys"]`.

**Negative.** The new tests fail against round 619's commit 0157df4:

```
    followup_neg_test.go:17: End 100: got 2..-28 ok false, want 2..29 (start + N, clamped to N-1)
--- FAIL: TestGraphKeysAreAMap
    followup_neg_test.go:43: keys [{1 16} {0 32} {0.5 48} {0 64}], want [{0 64} {0.5 48} {1 16}]
--- FAIL: TestStringNULAndHighBytes
    followup_neg_test.go:60: got "abc\x00def" "\xb7\xb9" tail 7
```

## Six-hundred-and-nineteenth round: 4,103 of the 4,170 particle effects now read completely, every value typed, ready for the effects renderer

The skills epic asked for "most of the particles loaded". Before this round, both `.efp` readers
walked a file as flat `(name, raw bytes)` pairs and decoded no values at all. They failed the
header of 854 files: 621 of those were version `0012`, and 165 had a root name that was not an
identifier. This round reads the client's own loader and implements it in both readers:
`server/internal/efp` `Decode` (Go) and `EfpReader.decode` (GDScript).
`docs/protocol/EFP_FORMAT.md` carries every layout with its address.

**READ (sro_client.exe, `/var/tmp/decomp_client` and `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm`):**
- **Header, `FUN_00cb8d70`.** The version is compared as a big-endian number. An f32 follows the
  magic from `0012`, and three u32 more from `0013`. Then comes the root node. So the old "u32
  before the name" was the root node's id (corrected in the follow-up above: it is HeadLen), and `0010` is laid out like `0011`.
- **Node, `FUN_00cc3a40`.** A node is: u32 id (HeadLen, per the follow-up), name, controllers (key + data), body, children.
- **Body, `FUN_00cc3500`.** A program (`u32 N` frames plus typed variables), six command lists,
  three single commands, a 20-byte block and a render block.
- **Commands, `FUN_00ca5460`.** Each is: u8 present, name, u8 space, u8 time flags, start, step,
  end, then the parameter when the registry gives the command a type.
- **Value types.** Each of the 16 types the registry `CGame::FUN_00ca0500` registers was
  followed from its factory to its vtable, and then to slot 5, the read. That gives each type's
  exact size, e.g. AxisVector4 16+64, RotVector 12+64, AngleVector1 24, the Frame* and Blend*
  graphs with their counts, and BSAnimation as `.ban` names.
- **Controllers.** The ten controllers' readers, from their classes' slot 3.
- **Timing, `FUN_00ca0f40`.** How a command's time flags turn start, step and end into a frame
  range over N.
- **Emission, `FUN_00c84e70`.** SEFStaticEmit is delay, duration, interval, count, quality (the last two corrected in the follow-up above: max_live and per_trigger).
- **Blending, `EFEffect::FUN_00cabda0`.** The node's 36-byte block is handed verbatim to Direct3D:
  cull, SRCBLEND, DESTBLEND, then colour and alpha arg1, arg2 and op on stage 0. This settles the
  spec's open blending question: blending is per node, not per texture name.

**MEASURED.** The census covers the retail `Particles.pk2` on the box, through `cmd/efpcensus`
and, identically, `client/tools/efp_census.gd`:

| | files |
|---|---|
| total | 4,170 |
| headers parsed | 4,103 (98.4 %) |
| tree decoded | 4,103 (98.4 %) |
| … to the exact byte | 4,096 |
| … zero padding after the root | 6 |
| … non-zero bytes after the root (`water_resurrection_effect_d`) | 1 |
| not decoded: `F8FILE` containers / `0000` files / empty files | 58 / 7 / 2 |

- **Every file whose header parses decodes, and the two readers agree.** Go and GDScript both
  count 4,103 decoded, 4,096 exact and 95,801 nodes.
- **The timing read is confirmed by the data.** A Frame* parameter holds exactly the number of keys
  FUN_00ca0f40 computes in 129,413 of 129,438 commands. The values are baked, one per key.
- **Blending.** Nodes blend additively (SRCALPHA/ONE) in 3,879 files and by alpha
  (SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA) in 2,007; 30 files use other pairs.
- **The census catches a wrong layout.** As a mutation check, AxisVector4 was read without its
  matrix, and decoded files fell from 4,103 to 784: exactly the files with no AxisVector4.
- **The `0000` files are not the node format.** The 7 of them fail with a string length of 5,385
  or more, and no skilleffect row names any. The readers reject them.

**OURS.** These choices are ours, not the client's:
- The readers reject versions outside the retail set, including `0000`. The client would read
  anything above `0013` as `0013`.
- An unknown command name fails. The client would skip its parameter and desynchronise.
- The allocation limits.
- The typed-tree API for round 620, documented at the top of `efp_reader.gd`. Per node it gives:
  frames, `loops()` / `never_extinct()`, `emission()`, `commands` / `command(name)` with
  `frame_range(n)`, `view_mode()`, `render_mode()`, `meshes`, the render `state` with
  `is_additive()`, and `vars`.

The existing callers are unaffected. `hit_effect.gd` and `level_up_effect.gd` scan the raw bytes
themselves, and `EfpReader.parse` keeps its API. The flat `parse` gained the header fixes and a
root-name rule that allows any bytes but control characters. It now accepts 4,103 files where the
base reader accepted 3,316 (MEASURED, both run over the same archive). Among the gains are
`system\system_levelup.efp` and its three copies, whose root name is EUC-KR Korean.

**Tests.**
- `efp_tree_test.gd` (101 checks) and the synthetic Go tests round-trip each of the 16 value
  types, a whole tree in every header version, every truncation and the frame-range rules.
- `TestRetailCensus` runs the census when `SRREVAMP_PARTICLES_PK2` is set; CI skips it.

## Six-hundred-and-eighteenth round: active buffs show by the HP bar, drain a time bar as they run out, burst when they end, and cancel on a right-click

The user asked for the skill icons that are active at the top left by the health bar. They wanted
a right-click to cancel one, and a way to see a buff about to expire, "check how the game
originally does that." The bar is now built: `client/scripts/ui/hud/hud_buff_board.gd`, placed at
`GDR_MAGICSTATEBOARD`'s own 220,10. It reads a skill's row through `skill_buff_catalog.gd`. The
full record, with every address, is `docs/protocol/magic_state_board.md`.

**How retail shows expiry** (READ, 0x8056a0): a 20 × 4 time bar under each icon drains from full
to empty. The fill is `s_stateodd_time_gauge.ddj` over the back `s_stateodd_time.ddj`, both 20 × 4
(MEASURED), at (total − elapsed) / total every frame. There is no blink. When a buff ends, a
9-frame `buf_effect.ddj` burst plays at 100 ms a tick, the icon fades by 0x55 a tick after tick 3,
`buf_disappear.wav` sounds, and the icon is removed at 900 ms. Right-click follows `vslot_033`:
- only the main list takes it;
- an icon that is already ending ignores it;
- `nbuf` without `lnks` does nothing;
- `cbuf` opens a 308 × 148 confirmation box;
- anything else calls `NetClient.send_buff_cancel`.

The tooltip is 0x800a10's format: "name Lv n", the description, and "Remaining time 45Second" /
"… 2Minute 5Second" / "Remaining time: 1Day 1Hour 1Minute", in the client's own words.

**Three things re-reading the decompile changed** from the spec, each READ:
- **An untimed buff shows no bar at all.** The spec said "full". The layout shows the gauge only
  when total ≠ −1 (asm 0x7ffd35..0x7ffd51). The per-frame update writes 1.0 into a hidden gauge.
- **A second-list (`bbuf`) buff that ends vanishes at once**, with no burst and no sound
  (0x804c60). The 0xB0BD handler always routes `bbuf` to that list: it passes param_4 = 0, asm
  0x8a5cbc.
- **A zero `dura` gets no icon** (0x7fda20). The add also takes the time left, so a buff joined
  midway starts part-drained (0x8048c0).

**The flags are the client's own data** (MEASURED). *Superseded by the review follow-up below:
the shard mapping, the run table and these counts were wrong.* `skilldata.txt` lists 47 shards
of 1000 ids each, and the bar loads the one a buff's id falls in. The Param block is walked with
the server's run table, copied into the client and guarded by a Go test. All 33,698 rows walk to
completion. The tags count: `cbuf` 473 (the spec's number), `nbuf` 285, `lnks` 308, `bbuf` 226.
Grass Walk A lv1 is id 113 and carries none of them.

**OURS / OPEN:**
- *(Superseded, see the review follow-up.)* The client is never told its own id, so the World3D
  hookup takes a buff as the player's when its owner is the sit-learned id, or failing that,
  neither another player's body nor a monster (OURS).
- The confirm box's text is OPEN, because retail passes an empty string. The box has the client's
  `UIIT_STT_CONFIRM_BOX` title and an empty body, in this client's confirm style (OURS). That its
  OK sends the cancel is INFERRED.
- The `lnks` frame, the red "Not affected" line and the "Target" line are not drawn (OPEN).
- The base's NetClient has no `buff_started`, `buff_ended` or `send_buff_cancel`; round 617 adds
  them. The board connects through `has_signal` / `has_method`, so until round 617 merges, only the
  new `SRREVAMP_QA_BUFFS` hook feeds it and a cancel logs "not sent".

**Measured.**
- `hud_buff_board_test.gd` passes: 68 checks over layout, gauge, routing (including a right press
  and release through the live viewport), end timing, tooltip, the walk and the QA hook. It covers
  every check the brief asked for.
- Against base b50a7b9 the suite cannot compile:
  - `SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Identifier "SkillBuffCatalog" not declared in the current scope.`
  - `SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Identifier "HudBuffBoard" not declared in the current scope.`
- With three rules mutated (the untimed gauge shown, `nbuf` ignoring `lnks`, the second list
  clickable) it fails as below. A fourth mutation, a plain `max(0, a − 0x55)` fade, behaves the
  same from 255 and fails nothing.
  - `FAIL untimed: the gauge is hidden (ShowWindow(total != -1))`
  - `FAIL nbuf with lnks -> cancel`
  - `FAIL second (bbuf) list -> nothing`
  - `FAIL nbuf and second-list clicks send nothing`
  - `FAIL plain click sends cancel(skill 1, token 21)`
- The Go drift test fails when one run length is changed:
  `client RUN["lnks"] = 4, Run = 5`.
- A live run on the box went through Login and CharSelect against an in-memory server. It had ten
  injected buffs, and `xdotool` sent real X right-clicks. The log shows:
  - the plain icon routed to `cancel` ("not sent", the base has no sender);
  - the `nbuf` icon and the `bbuf` icon to `none`;
  - the `cbuf` icon to `confirm`;
  - `0` SCRIPT ERRORs.

  The frames show the bar, the tooltip ("Grass Walk - Flow Lv 1 / Increases the character's … /
  Remaining time 41Second"), the confirmation box and a burst mid-play. They show; they do not
  prove.

**Review follow-up.** The branch was merged with round 617 (feat/selfcast) and adapted to it. Each
fix below has its own test.
- **Right-click is hit-tested at the release** (READ, vslot_033 tests where the button comes up).
  The slot's rect is 20 × 24, the icon plus its gauge (0x806d50 sizes it). A press on one icon and
  a release on another cancels the other; a release off every icon does nothing.
- **The board is cleared** on every successful `enter_world_result`, which covers re-entry and a
  character switch. Nothing bursts or sounds.
- **Whose buff it is** now uses round 617's real signals:
  - `buff_started(SkillNet.BuffStart)` and `buff_ended(SkillNet.BuffEnd)`;
  - a start is this player's when its ownerKind is 0 and its owner id is `_sync_own_id`'s
    (OpSelfId, else the sit answer). With no id, nothing is shown;
  - an end is matched by token alone;
  - a cancel goes to `NetClient.send_buff_cancel`.
- **The skill rows come from retail's list.** `Client_LoadAllRefData` (0x844cd0) loads
  `skilldataenc.txt`, which names `SkillData_1000ENC` … `47000ENC`. The files overlap:
  - the 5000-wide ones repeat the 1000-wide ones below them;
  - `35000` holds 30000–46422;
  - 38000–43000 are empty.

  So the first build's mapping missed every id only a wide file holds, among them every id from
  37000 to 44147. The ENC files are encrypted: a `"\r\n//encrypt"` trailer, and 0x4f5140 adds
  `T2[k % 0xa7] − T1[k % 0x1ef]` to each byte, k = 0x8c1f + file offset. The key tables live in
  the executable at 0xeae758 / 0xeae948 and are not copied into the repo. Decrypted on the box,
  the ENC set is 33,632 ids, and its 27,714 duplicated ids all agree.

  The catalog now indexes the plain twins in list order, with a duplicate going to its first
  file. Checked by the catalog itself against every decrypted ENC row: 0 missing and 0 differences
  in tags, level, icon, name or description. The plain files' one disagreeing duplicate, 35958,
  agrees with ENC under first-wins.
- **The run table is the client's**, from its own parser 0x9bbca0: 188 codes. `bldr` is 5 (the

## Six-hundred-and-seventeenth round: Grass Walk and the self-buffs cast with nothing selected, and Ghost Walk casts at a point picked on the ground

"Some skills don't require you attack a monster like grass walk, ghost walk, and a bunch of
buffs." The client refused every one of them: `World3D._cast_skill` answered "Select a target
first" whenever nothing was selected, before the skill's own columns were looked at. This round is
the client half of the skills epic (rounds 616-619; the shared contract is in
`docs/protocol/auto_command.md`, "srrevamp's cast and buff messages").

**What decides it (READ).** The skill tick (server `0x4ae590`, phase 0) sends a row with
Target_Required 0 (skilldata col 22), or Target_Required 1 with TargetType_Land 1 (col 24), straight
to the cast with no approach. The client already read both columns for the approach walk
(`HudPanels.skill_reach`); it now keeps them, and `SelfCast.plan` (new, `scripts/world/self_cast.gd`)
decides:
- **Target_Required 0** (Grass Walk 113, the imbues, the shields, the self-heals; 669 kind-3 and 80
  kind-0 China rows, skills_spec §1.5, MEASURED earlier): OpUseSkill **targetType 0** at once, from
  where the player stands, with the cast clip and cast sounds on the player. A selected monster
  stays selected and is not re-shown as the target.
- **Target_Required 1 + Land 1** (Ghost Walk 114, the 19 rows): **ground-pick mode**. The next left
  click on the world takes its point from the click-to-move ray (`_ground_point_at`, factored out of
  `_try_set_move_target`) and sends **targetType 2** with it; the click does not also walk, attack or
  talk. Right click or Escape cancels (Escape is read in `_input`, before HudPanels would close a
  window or open the System menu with it). The cursor is the system cross -- **OURS**; retail's
  ground-cast cursor and decal were not read (OPEN).
- Everything else: the old flow (walk into reach, then cast at the selection; refused with none).

**The reply is not a blow (OURS).** srrevamp's server still answers a cast with OpAttackResult, and
World3D drew every reply as a hit on the selected monster -- a swing, a flinch, the counter. NetClient
now tags each reply with the targetType of the request it answers (a queue in step with the
existing in-flight target queue; `AttackResult.target_type`), and a type-0/2 reply with no damage is
logged and dropped by `_on_attack_result` (the HP bar still takes its HP). A monster cast still in
flight keeps its hit effect, and the selection is untouched. A self cast's monster field carries the
selection when there is one, so a server that predates the type byte reach-gates a damaging
Target_Required 0 row against it as before (OURS; disclosed in the contract doc).

**The new messages.** SkillNet decodes OpBuffStart 0x00F5, OpBuffEnd 0x00F6 and OpSkillMove 0x00F8
exactly per the contract, NetClient emits them as `buff_started`, `buff_ended` and `skill_moved`
(documented at the top of `net_client.gd` for round 618), and `send_buff_cancel(skill_id, token)`
encodes OpBuffCancel 0x00F7. World3D applies a buff's `runSpeed` (0 = unchanged) to `_move_speed`,
which is the characterdata Speed2 value the client already moves by (round 231; the server does not
police speed), so the two agree in units. OpSkillMove **snaps** this player to the point -- the move's
duration is OPEN (`tele` value[0] = 500 is not read by the server's clamp) -- and puts another
player's body there. The client is not told its own character id (MonsterStrikes has the same gap),
so it LEARNS it: a start or move for a skill it cast within 10 s (OURS), naming no other player drawn
here, is its own; an end is its own when its owner is that id or it ends a claimed token.

That server predates round 616: it accepts both casts as non-damaging rows and sends no buff start,

**Review follow-up.** The review found five things; the contract gained four trailing fields
for them (`docs/protocol/auto_command.md`), and round 616's server is told the same:
- **A self cast's reply drawn as a blow, and a death swallowed.** The reply's type came from a
  FIFO of sent requests, which a server keep-up repeat (sent unasked) or a swing dropped inside
  its re-use delay puts out of step: mid-fight the repeat took the self cast's 0, and a 0-damage
  repeat on which the monster killed the player was swallowed as the cast's reply. OpAttackResult
  now echoes the request's targetType as a trailing u8 (a repeat sends 1), read into
  `AttackResult.target_type` / `target_type_echoed`; the queue only fills a reply that carries no
  echo, and such a reply is swallowed only when it carries no damage, kill, death or error. Even
  echoed, a death is always drawn.
- **Own id.** OpSelfId 0x00F9 `{i64 characterId}` on world entry, NetClient
  `self_id_received(character_id)` and `own_character_id` (reset on connect, disconnect and each
  enter_world). `World3D._sync_own_id` gives it to SelfCast and to the sit state, logging a
  disagreement with an id either had learned; before one arrives the sit answer's id is used, and
  the learn-from-own-cast heuristic is the last fallback only. OpBuffStart/End carry a trailing
  ownerKind: a monster's buff (kind 1) is never this player's, whatever its id.
- **Cursor leak.** A pick left on when the world leaves (`_exit_tree`) or the session ends
  (`_on_disconnected`, which the System menu's Restart and Exit reach) is cancelled and the
  default shape reset (`_leave_ground_pick`).
- **Orphaned comment.** `_on_state_changed`'s doc comment is back on its function.
- **Hit effect of a Target_Required 0 `att` row cast at a selection.** Not restored: once a
  server applies a type-0 cast to the caster the effect has no target. What is pinned is that an
  echoed type-0, no-damage reply naming the selection is a quiet accept (no swing, selection kept).

"Some skills don't require you attack a monster like grass walk, ghost walk, and a bunch of

## Six-hundred-and-fifteenth round: windows swoosh where the original's do, the item and level-up sounds play, and the Option window's Audio page sets the three volumes

"Some interface elements when opened make a swoosh sound." They are `uiwinopen.wav` /
`uiwinclose.wav`, played by one toggle helper (0x79a7e0) that a window's routine calls after it
has shown or hid the window. Rather than put a swoosh on every window, each of this client's
windows was checked against its retail routine (the table is in `docs/protocol/SOUND_FORMAT.md`,
"Interface sounds"): the popup's tab keys, M, E, T, Y, Escape, close buttons and the NPC shop and
warehouse sound; **Q, U and the NPC talk box's opening are silent in retail** (their routines
only ShowWindow), and so are ordinary buttons. A key that switches the tab of the popup already
up sounds the open again (read, 0x79b062).

Three things the plan had assumed turned out otherwise, each settled by reading the code:
`snd_revive` is a broken item being repaired, not the player's resurrection (0x8adf50);
`snd_button_click` is the title screen's server list, not its confirm (message map 0xec36d8,
control id 51 of pstitle.txt); and `snd_pickup` is named by no code at all -- the character
`.bsr` pick-up animations carry it (measured with pk2grep), so it is the animation round's.

The Option window is the one the button really opens: `res_ui\optionwnd.2dt` (CNIFOption,
0x6f5190), not the `ifoption_audio.txt` layout the research note named -- that family is
declared but never opened by the button. It opens on Video (0x600850); the Audio tab has the
three sliders (0..100, travel 452 px, the thumb at prev + 1 + v*452/100) and mute boxes, bound
to `AudioOptions`; Default is 50/50/50 (0x5f6660, not the 30/50/50 first-run defaults).

Measured: `ui_sounds_test.gd` passes (and fails 6 against 23baaf0); the client suite runs 129
suites, 0 failing; a live run against the server pressed I, S, M, T, Q, U and Escape through
push_input and logged the `AUDIO ui` lines. Open: RARE drops, wear sounds, quest/elixir/socket
sounds (no such events here), the exchange's close button, the Option window's other tabs.

## Six-hundred-and-fourteenth round: a blow sounds when it lands -- the sword's own hit, a critical's crack, a block's clang -- and a skill plays its own cast sounds

**Built** (`docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`, round 614; `docs/protocol/SOUND_FORMAT.md`, "Combat and
skill sounds"): the code-fired half of the combat audio. When the player's blow lands, retail's
key for it plays at the player (the attacker): `PLAYER:snd_cridmg:-:-:-:-` for a critical, else
`PLAYER:snd_dmg:<skill group>:-:-:-` -- a plain swing carries the weapon's base attack
(`SKILL_CH_SWORD_BASE`), a Smash its own group. A blocked counter plays
`PLAYER:snd_blocking:-:-:NORMAL|CRITYCAL:-` at the blocker. A cast plays its skilleffectset
SndBegin files at the caster: READY and the first SHOT rows as it starts, the second SHOT rows as
the blow lands, `snd_activate` and the ACT_S / ACT_L rows when the server accepts it.
`SkillAudio.set_current` / `context_of` give the animation-fired swings and voices the player's
current skill.

**Found, not guessed:** the weapon fallback key is built with five tokens
(`PLAYER:snd_dmg:SWORD:-:NORMAL`, asm 0xa70b10-0xa70b43), so it never matches the table's
six-token weapon rows; the research had written six. In retail every blow carries a skill, so the
group key is what sounds -- and a bare hand (group `SKILL_PUNCH` against rows keyed
`SKILL_PUNCH_BASE`) is silent. Monster hits are keyed by the monster's attack skill, which
srrevamp's server does not send: logged and silent.

**Measured live** on the box: `AUDIO hit: PLAYER:snd_dmg:SKILL_CH_SWORD_BASE:-:-:-`, `AUDIO crit:
PLAYER:snd_cridmg:-:-:-:-`, `AUDIO hit: PLAYER:snd_dmg:SKILL_CH_SWORD_SMASH_A:-:-:- ... (skill 3 on
monster 15, 36 damage)`, `AUDIO cast READY/-1: prim\snd\skill\csk_heal_ready.wav` and `AUDIO cast
ACT_S/-1: prim\snd\skill\csk_heal_nega.wav` for the water self-heal. A cast is paired with the
first result after it, so a fast-loop swing already in flight took one Smash's keys; the log
shows it.

**Negatives:** on 23baaf0 both suites FAIL on the missing scripts and World3D's missing hooks;
planted bugs (a six-token weapon key, a block without CRITYCAL) FAIL four named checks. 130
suites, 0 failing.

**Review follow-up:** SndEnd is read -- it plays with SndBegin, in the same call -- and rows with
only a SndEnd are kept; a dangling Basic_Original keys as `-`, as retail's walk does; a plain swing
sounds at 0 damage and a blocked blow plays the attacker's hit too (retail makes the damage
decoration for every record); the attacker side and the block's CRITYCAL are now READ.

## Six-hundred-and-tenth round: open ground repeats every 80 units and the region lightmap shades it, so dirt no longer reads as a grid

**Report** (Jangan, HUD X:6431 Y:978): the dirt "has an extreme tile look" and four textures show
on a path that should be dirt. A retail screenshot of the same spot then settled the path: the
user withdrew it; the textures there are right and were not changed.

**Read from the retail client** (addresses and assembly in `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`, round 610):
retail draws the ground fixed-function, one pass per TextureInfo of a block. The tile's texcoord
is `(col, row) * 0.25` per block vertex (`SWorld::vslot_035`, `0x9f03f0`, the double 0.25) --
**one repeat per 80 world units** -- then a stage-1 texture matrix picked by the TextureInfo's top
three bits scales it by 1, 0.5, 0.25, 2 or 4 (5-7: zero), built in `0x00a2f370`. After the tile
passes every block is drawn again multiplying the framebuffer by `min(1, lightmap +
TerrainShadowColor)`, the region's `.t` lightmap on its own inset UV (`Map::FUN_00a18d10`,
ZERO/SRCCOLOR, stage 0 ADD of texture and TFACTOR; the TFACTOR is environment channel 6, placed by
`Map::FUN_00a1b650`'s read order).

**Measured** (`client/tools/measure_ground_tiling.gd`): the spot is `97\168.m` cell (col 47,
row 9); 63 of its 64 surrounding vertices are ID 11 `c_dust_hmfld_03`, top bits 0. **We repeated
that texture every 20 units, four times retail's rate.** Bits 10-12 of the TextureInfo are 0 at
every vertex of 97/168, 96/168, 98/168 and 100/100. And the `.t` lightmap, applied as an AO texture
since 2026-08-23, has not shown on the baked (unshaded) terrain since round 71: AO is a lighting
input, and Godot hides `ao_texture` on an unshaded material. The multiplier darkens 44% of 97/168's texels.

**Fix**: `MapmTerrainBuilder.TEXCOORD_PER_VERTEX` 0.25 and `TEXTURE_MATRIX_SCALES` replace round
69's one-repeat-per-quad; the lightmap term (`lightmap_term`, with `_env_terrain_shadow` from
World3D) is each terrain material's MUL detail layer on retail's UV2 (`lightmap_coord`). The flat
base's render priority (round 580) is untouched.

**Negative**: `mapm_terrain_builder_test.gd` against e39e00b -- 8 failures, among them
`FAIL every opaque-pass vertex carries the read UV (col, row) * 0.25 * scale[top bits] (30719 of
36864 wrong; first: vertex (r 0, c 1) has (1, 0), want (0.25, 0))` and `FAIL the builder has the
retail lightmap term and coordinate`; ALL PASS here. `remote_godot.sh check` 314 scripts ALL LOAD;
`tests` 122 suites, 0 failing; Go build and `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` green. Entry benchmark:
grid 16,976 -> 17,078 ms, off-thread terrain +33 ms a region (the lightmap term).

**Not changed, open**: retail's blend (the lowest-key corner claims a quad opaque and bleeds into
its neighbours; ours takes the most-used corner), its alternating quad diagonals, its

## Six-hundred-and-seventh round: N sits down and stands up, and sitting regenerates HP and MP at the client's rate

The full record is `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s entry of the same name (round 607); the protocol page
is `docs/protocol/opcodes/motion.md`.

- **The formula (read).** `CGObjPC::vslot_362` restores `trunc(MaxHP x hprg / 100)`, floored at 1,
  clamped to `[0, trunc(MaxHP x 0.5)]`, MP the same with `mprg`, every 4 s on the character's own
  timer (first tick 4 s after it is made; sitting does not re-arm it), only in STAND or SIT.
  `SetMotionState` (`0x4a9d00`) writes `hprg`/`mprg` = **8.0 sitting, 0.8 otherwise**. The pool is
  the **maximum**: slot `0x110` in `CGObjPC`'s vtable is `0x4a6830` = `ftol(EvaluateParam(3))`.
  The 4%-of-current rule that shipped since 2026-09-16 was own design on a misread slot, and the
  "hprg is only written by skills" census had missed SetMotionState; both records are corrected.
- **The request (read).** `0x704f` is handler `0x04f` -> `0x4b1450` -> `FUN_004b1480`: a toggle
  through 1.5 s of CHANGEMOTION, then `0x30bf {id, 1, value}`. `0x7021`'s handler refuses a move
  only in states 8, `0x10`, `0x12`, so **a move while seated is accepted and stands at once**; a
  blow stands a sitter; the skill gate refuses a seated cast only for the 59 skills carrying
  `ao`/`pw` or a kind-1 `msch` (corrected in the follow-up below; the first commit refused every
  swing and cast).
- **The clips (measured).** Types 13/14/15 from the body's `.bsr`: `chinaman_a_sitground` /
  `_sitbreath` / `_sitstand` for the man, `chinawoman_a_*` for the woman.
- **Live (measured, `/var/tmp/rsit/live4.log`).** MaxHP/MaxMP 568: standing **+4 HP, +4 MP** a
  tick, sitting **+45 HP** a tick (MP 547 -> 568, capped), +4 again after standing up; `Bip01
  Pelvis` 9.2 above the feet standing, 0.93 seated. The log lines are in the RE_COMPLETION entry.
- **Ours, disclosed:** walking is an accepted OpMove under 0.5 s old (the server has no WALK
  state); this client learns its own id from the answer to its own N; the id is the character id
  in the u32; the refusal text; the regen poll of 100 ms.
- **Open:** other players' sit was not seen live (tested over the wire); the retail client's
  handling of a click or swing while seated is unread; the Action window's Sit/Stand label has no
  window to go in here.
- **Follow-up after review (second commit).** The seated-cast refusal is now the READ one: only
  skills carrying `ao`/`pw` (58 rows: the Cold/Fire walls, the fortress repair kits) or a kind-1
  `msch` (the monster transform) are refused, via the exporter's new `SitGate` column; a plain or
  duel swing is not refused and the attacker stays seated. Regen runs under the kill lock and skips
  HP 0 (a lethal blow's kill could be dropped; the window is narrowed, not closed, and MP still
  regenerates at HP 0); a move while seated is sent at once (a tap left
  client and server disagreeing); newcomers are told who sits; the own-id window expires. Stale
  records ("no passive regen", "an item stat", "1 point does not regenerate", the dead tracker)
  corrected in place. Time to full from 50% at MaxHP 568: 76 s before, 284 s standing, 28 s
  sitting; nothing regenerates while moving. Negatives against b62e19c in the RE_COMPLETION entry.
- **Second follow-up (third commit).** Renumbered 607 after dev's keys rounds. Players already
  sitting are drawn seated: the enter-world and zone-change results carry a `Seated` tail, because a
  separate `0x30bf` behind them was measured arriving before any body could take it (the previous
  commit's `tellSeated`, removed). Live: two bots seated in jangan and donwhang, the client entering
  one and `/goto`-ing to the other -- `SIT: player 2 drawn seated on spawn` and `player 1`.
  `deploy/README.md` says srrevamp-01 must re-export, re-import and restart before the skill gate
  works (until then it fails open). Regen's stats push leaves the lock first; alive at HP 0 still
  gets MP; the kill window is narrowed, not closed. Seated fighting at 8% is recorded as a
  consequence of the read server gate, the retail client's side unread.
- **Third follow-up (fourth commit).** A regen stats push built outside the kill lock could land
  after a lethal blow and draw a live HP bar on a dead character; the server now re-checks life
  and HP right before the send, and the client ignores a stats HP while dead. The spawn test now
  checks the loop clip each body plays, through the real `_on_change_zone_result`. The Seated tail

## Six-hundred-and-fifth round: The keys work again after a line of chat, once the player clicks the HUD

The full record is `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s entry of the same name (round 605).

- **Report.** v0.1.451: "the keyboard shortcuts stopped working"; v0.1.450 was fine. Which keys and
  when were not said.
- **The plain path works (measured).** A new hook, `SRREVAMP_QA_INPUT`, plays clicks and keys into
  the real world through `push_input`, with keycode, physical keycode, label and character set.
  Six live runs on d4d1303 at 1280x720 all toggled their windows. The runs covered: I C K U Q M Y P
  A L, the number keys, F1/F2, Escape, and the same key again to close; clicks inside the popup,
  guild, quest, map and alchemy windows; the bar's buttons and its menu; hovering for tooltips; the
  talk box; `--server`; the real loading screen; a second entry through Login and CharacterSelect.
  A headless sweep with the real Media.pk2 clicked every clickable control of every window, the
  bar, the minimap and the player block, 363 in all. After each click an unbound key still reached
  the unhandled stage, except while the party-match window's own search fields had the keyboard.
- **What breaks them (measured).** A line of chat, then a click on the HUD. The chat line keeps the
  keyboard after Enter. On d4d1303 a click on the bar's inventory button or its menu left the focus
  in the chat, and K, C, I and Q were typed into it. On v0.1.450 (the same hook in a copy), a click
  on the bar's community button moved the focus to the button, and K and C opened their windows.
- **Why.** Until rounds 595-604 the bar and the windows were UiBuilder TextureButtons, which are
  FOCUS_ALL, so any click on them took the keyboard from the chat. The rebuilt bar, its menu, the
  guild, quest, map and alchemy windows (TwoDtBuilder) and every close button are FOCUS_NONE. Only
  a click on the open world gave the keyboard back (`World3D.take_focus_back`).
- **Fix.** `HudPanels.release_text_focus_on_press`, first in `HudPanels._input`: a left press
  releases a focused text line unless it lands on the line itself or on the HUD surface that holds
  it. That surface is a window, or a child of the HUD container such as the chat, and it must be
  the topmost surface under the press. The press is not consumed. A window drawn over the chat
  takes the keyboard. A click on the chat's scrollback, a right press or the wheel keeps it (round
  522). That the retail client does the same was not read.
- **Negative.** `hud_keys_after_chat_test.gd` drives the chat, the bar, its menu and the quest
  window with `push_input` only. On d4d1303: 8 FAIL. Here: ALL PASS. Live on this tree, the same
  chat-then-bar run opens skill with K and character with C.

## Five-hundred-and-ninety-fourth round: the client reads the retail .2dt window files

The newer windows of the retail client (guild and community, quest list, enchant, world-map
guide, the menu bar and the rest) are binary `res_ui\*.2dt` files, not `resinfo\if*.txt`
layouts. The full record is `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s entry of the same name, and
`docs/protocol/2DT_FORMAT.md` is the spec.

- **Format, read.** A `u32` count, then 976-byte records (0x48f983, `push 0x3d0` at 0x48f9b5),
  nothing else. The reader refuses any other size. Parents are linked by (parent, grandparent),
  because ids repeat, over the same file's earlier windows (0x48cb00, the file check at 0x48cbce).
- **Newly read.** `on` is a tab's checked piece (0x47a387 / 0x47a2f7). A check box's `off` is the
  box and its `on` the mark (0x482ef2 / 0x482f2c). Windows start visible (0xb9e284).
  CNIFMainFrame's chrome is CIFMainFrame's numbers (0x479a50).
- **Inferred, and labelled so.** The colour is the text colour, never a tint. The alignment
  bytes' 0 / 1 / 2 meaning is the `.txt` path's. The sample text at 0x300 is never drawn.
- **Measured** (`client/tools/check_2dt_files.gd`, new): 42 files, 2312 records, all exact. 2310
  links resolve, and 2 have parent 0. None is ambiguous. All strings are ASCII. 2555 of 2555
  required pieces exist. Tiles precede the content they overlap in 690 of 694 sibling pairs.
- **Tests.** `twodt_reader_test.gd` on synthetic bytes fails twice against fcd0b08 (the scripts
  do not exist) and passes here. 110 suites, 0 failing. Go: 59 packages ok.
- **Open.** The draw loop, the alignment values, how an off-size textured static is drawn (80 of
  283), and the classes' own art for edit, combo, scroll, page and spin controls.

## Five-hundred-and-eighty-third round: seasonal event decorations (Christmas, Halloween, the open-beta event, the summer festival) are hidden by default

The user decided on 2026-09-26 that early testing gets no seasonal decorations, and chose four
sets. `SeasonalObjects` names a placed piece's set by the folder in its Map.pk2 `object.ifo` path,
never by id: id 3297 sits between two Halloween ids and is `arabia_fouad`. The rules are
`\etc\x_mas\`, `res\etc\halloween\`, `res\etc\obt\obt_event` and `res\etc\summer_event\`.
`World3D._objects_prepare` drops those placements after the de-duplication and before the ownership
step and the model loop. Their models are never read, and their collision goes with them.
`SRREVAMP_SEASONAL=christmas,...` or `seasonal="christmas,..."` under `[world]` in
`settings.cfg` shows a set again. The value must be quoted, or the whole file fails to parse. No
window writes that setting yet. No switch was found in the client's `.o2` loader, so this is our
choice. The
full record, with the layer tables that ground the folder-to-event mapping, is
`docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 583.

- **Measured on the box**, with World3D's own job and prepare over the real archive
  (`client/tools/probe_seasonal.gd`). Hidden per region as christmas/halloween/obt/summer:
  96/168 1/9/0/0, 97/167 5/12/5/5, 97/168 26/34/25/30, 97/169 6/15/5/5, 98/167 4/5/3/3 and
  98/169 3/6/0/0. The other three of Jangan's nine have none. That is the investigation's
  table, plus one record in 98/169: a list-2 Halloween piece owned by 97/169, which the filter
  counts because it runs before the ownership step. After the prepare, no seasonal placement is
  left in any of the nine. With `SRREVAMP_SEASONAL=christmas`, 97/168 gets back exactly its 26
  Christmas pieces. No Jangan `.nvm` record is seasonal (0 of 600), so navigation is unchanged.
- **Found in the loader** (`FUN_00a361b0`; `docs/protocol/MAPO2_FORMAT.md` is corrected). An
  `.o2` record's bytes 22-23 are its uid and bytes 28-29 its owner region. Byte 27 bit 0 makes
  retail skip the record. In the 4,559 region `.o2` files, 240 list-2 records set that bit, and
  we draw them: `bagh_masin_lightwall` (120), guild barricades (48), Baghdad's event barricades
  (46), Petra's fires (24) and `res\dun\jupiter\piety\piety_golddoor.bsr` (2). None is in
  Jangan and none is seasonal. That is open in `docs/TODO.md`.
- **Review corrections, folded into the records.**
  - There are 878 seasonal `.o2` entries, not 868. The scan covers the region files only; the 15
    root `.o2` files were not scanned.
  - `sro_client.exe` does hold five `UIIT_MSG_XMAS_EVENT_*` UI strings. It has no folder or
    layer-file string.
  - The layer join is now stated with its method: by position, within 0.05 on every axis, one
    count per distinct row, 929 rows. It gives layer 7 233 Christmas rows, 4-5 12 + 202
    Halloween, 8-9 15 + 304 OBT and 1 91 summer. `alex_burner` matches no layer row.
